What should MSgt Rush find?

answers.text: The routes are removed from the table
answers.rationale: Entries are removed only after 240 seconds without an update, and that time has not yet passed.

answers.text: The routes are kept and still used
answers.rationale: Once 180 seconds or more pass without an update, the routes are no longer in use.

answers.text: The routes are marked as unusable
answers.rationale: Routes served by a device silent for 180 seconds or more are marked unusable before removal at 240 seconds.

answers.text: The routes are advertised as new
answers.rationale: Advertising is the sending of updates every 30 seconds by a working device, not by the silent router.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's workstation starts a session with a file server, and a virtual port is allocated on both the client and server sides for that session. Data moves between them for several minutes, and then the session is complete. MSgt Rush then checks what has happened to the virtual port that the session used on the workstation. What should MSgt Rush find?

answers.rationale: Dynamically opened ports stay open only for the session and are closed or released once it completes.

answers.text: It stays open for the next session
answers.rationale: These ports are specific to one session, so they do not remain open after it ends.

answers.text: It is kept as a registered port
answers.rationale: Registered ports are assigned for specific application services, not kept from a finished session.
Well-known ports are assigned to common protocols and services, not taken from finished sessions.

questions.stem: A software company builds a new remote management application for squadron computers and asks the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) for an official port number so that the application always listens on the same one. The application is not one of the common protocols and services that system processes use. From which port range can the company receive that assignment?

answers.rationale: These ports are assigned to common protocols and services for system processes, which this application is not.
These ports cannot be registered with the authority; they are assigned as needed and then released.
All ports are virtual paths for data; this is not one of the three numbered ranges.
This range is assigned by the authority for specific application services, which fits the company's request.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush builds a table of the open ports on a squadron server. Next to each port number, MSgt Rush adds an entry such as email transfer, webpage delivery, or file copying, so that the table shows what each open port is there to do. Which term names what MSgt Rush is recording in those entries?

keywords.text: what each open port is there to do

answers.rationale: Port status is only open or closed, not what a port is used to do.
The purpose for which a port is used is called a service.
A protocol is a set of rules for communicating, not the purpose assigned to a port.
A header is information a layer adds to data, not a port's purpose.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush traces a Web page request down the five-layer model on a workstation. The Network Layer has just created a packet and passed it to the Data Link Layer (DLL), which will hand its own result to the Physical Layer for transmission. Which information does the Data Link Layer place in the header it adds at this step?

answers.rationale: The Transport Layer adds source and destination port numbers in its header, before the Network Layer step.

answers.text: Source and destination Internet Protocol (IP) addresses
answers.rationale: The Network Layer already added these addresses when it created the packet.

answers.text: Packet sequence number and port information
answers.rationale: The Transport Layer adds the packet sequence number used for Transmission Control Protocol (TCP).

answers.text: Source and destination Media Access Control (MAC) addresses
answers.rationale: The Data Link Layer (DLL) adds a header containing the source and destination hardware addresses to create a frame.

questions.stem: An airman sends an email message with a large attachment using Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP). Partway through the transfer, one piece of the data never reaches the destination email server, although the rest arrives. Which result does the type of delivery that SMTP relies on produce for the missing piece?

answers.rationale: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) relies on Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), so data not received is re-sent by the sender.

answers.text: The loss is tolerated and ignored
answers.rationale: Tolerating minor packet loss fits connectionless delivery, which this email protocol does not rely on.

answers.text: It is broadcast to each host
answers.rationale: Broadcast is a User Datagram Protocol (UDP) transmission method, not how missing email data is recovered.

answers.text: It is resolved by the server
answers.rationale: Resolving converts addresses; it does not recover data that never reached the destination.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush prepares a printed list of Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) addresses for the printers in a building. The network reads each address as one long string of binary bits, but the airmen who use the list need each address shown in a more user-friendly manner. Which format should MSgt Rush use for the list?

answers.rationale: This format represents a binary Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) address in a more user-friendly manner.
Preferred notation writes Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) addresses as hexadecimal groups.
Mixed notation combines Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) and Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) values in one address.
Compressed notation shortens Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) addresses by removing zero strings.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sets up a training video stream that must reach only a set of designated recipients, not every host on the network. Each airman's workstation that should receive the stream joins the group first, and the stream is addressed to that group membership rather than to one host. Which address class is reserved for the addresses this stream uses?

answers.rationale: Class E is reserved for research and development.
Class D is reserved for multicast addressing to designated recipients.
Class C is used for small networks of individual hosts.
Class A is used for large networks of individual hosts.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reviews the address plan for a very large organization network that must hold the largest number of hosts. In each address of the plan, only the first octet identifies the network, and the remaining three octets identify the host or node. Which address class matches this plan?

answers.rationale: Class B serves intermediate-sized networks and gives more of the address to the network.
Class C serves small networks and leaves the host only the last octet.
Class A uses the first octet for the network and the remaining octets for the host.
Class D is reserved for multicast and has no host field.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's squadron receives one public address from its Internet Service Provider (ISP), yet hundreds of new workstations must join the internal company subnet. MSgt Rush wants each workstation to have its own address for internal use, while all traffic on the Internet sees the single public address. Which kind of address lets the network administrators extend the network this way?

answers.text: Automatic Private Internet Protocol (IP) Addressing (APIPA) addresses
answers.rationale: These self-assigned addresses should not be used for private networks.
Loopback addresses keep traffic within one computer for testing.

answers.text: Class E addresses for each workstation
answers.rationale: Class E addresses are reserved for research and development.
Private Internet Protocol (IP) addresses let administrators extend networks behind one public address.

questions.stem: An airman's laptop is set to obtain its address automatically and has no static address configured. Overnight the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server goes offline, and the next morning the laptop cannot obtain a lease. The laptop now shows an address that no administrator set and no server issued. Which addressing produced that address?

answers.rationale: The host auto-assigns itself this address when no static address or lease is available.

answers.text: Private Internet Protocol (IP) addressing from a reserved range
answers.rationale: Private ranges are reserved for internal networks, not self-assigned by a host.

answers.text: Loopback addressing reserved for testing in the computer
answers.rationale: Loopback addresses keep traffic inside the computer for testing.

answers.text: Class D addressing reserved for group members
answers.rationale: Class D addresses are reserved for multicast to designated recipients.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is debugging a new program on a workstation and wants the program to send and receive its own packets. The data must be processed by the protocol stack inside the same computer and must not be transmitted out into the network to be routed. Which address should the program send its data to?

keywords.text: send and receive its own packets

answers.text: The Automatic Private Internet Protocol (IP) Addressing (APIPA) address
answers.rationale: Automatic Private Internet Protocol (IP) Addressing (APIPA) addresses are self-assigned when no lease is available.

answers.text: The loopback address of the computer
answers.rationale: The loopback address, the local host, keeps traffic within the computer.
A private address identifies a host on the company subnet, not a local test path.

answers.text: A Class D multicast group address
answers.rationale: Class D addresses reach designated recipients on the network.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is writing a long Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) address in compressed notation. The address holds two separate long strings of zero groups, one near the start and one near the end. MSgt Rush wants the shortened address to follow the substitution rules. How should the double colon be applied?

answers.text: Use a double colon in each of the two zero strings
answers.rationale: A given address may hold that symbol one time, not in each string.

answers.text: Use a single colon in place of each zero string
answers.rationale: A single colon separates groups and does not mark compressed zeros.

answers.text: Use a double colon for only one of the zero strings
answers.rationale: The double colon can be used one time in any given address.

answers.text: Use mixed notation to replace both zero strings
answers.rationale: Mixed notation combines Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) and Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) values; it does not compress zeros.

questions.stem: An airman sorts a list of network addresses by class, reading the value in each first octet. One entry is written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits separated by colons, an Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) address. The airman asks MSgt Rush which class to record for that entry. What should MSgt Rush tell the airman?

keywords.text: sorts a list of network addresses by class

answers.text: Record it as Class E, reserved for research
answers.rationale: Class E is an Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) class reserved for research and development.

answers.text: Record it as Class D, reserved for multicast
answers.rationale: Class D is an Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) class reserved for multicast addressing.

answers.text: Record it by the class of its first group
answers.rationale: Classes come from an Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) first octet value, not hexadecimal groups.

answers.text: Record it as having no class
answers.rationale: Unlike Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4), there are no classes in Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6).

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds a value made only of ones and zeros printed in an old manual, and an airman cannot tell whether it is a binary, decimal, or hexadecimal number. A small number written as a subscript beside the value would settle the question by identifying the number system. Which part of a number is that subscript?

answers.rationale: The Most Significant Digit (MSD) carries the most weight at the left of a number.
The radix, written as a subscript, is the base of the number system.
A place holder zero keeps digits in their correct positions.
The Least Significant Digit (LSD) carries the least weight at the right.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must keep two fully functional Local Area Networks (LANs) in hospital blocks on opposite sides of a city connected if the buried fiber between them is cut. The plan allows no new cable runs between the buildings and no cellular subscriptions for the link equipment. Which wireless network type fits this backup link between the two hospital blocks?

answers.rationale: A Wireless Wide Area Network (WWAN) needs devices provisioned with a service provider subscription, which the plan rules out.
This type connects blocks of a hospital, serves as a backup for wired networks and links two independent network nodes.
A Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) covers a limited area such as one building, not blocks across a city.
A hybrid network plugs wired devices into a hybrid router's ports; it does not link distant buildings.

questions.stem: An airman's new tablet must stay on the network from a vehicle while driving between installations across a whole region. At a public hotspot the tablet joins without trouble, but on the road it connects only after MSgt Rush has it provisioned with a subscription from a cellular service provider. Which wireless network type serves the tablet on the road?

answers.rationale: A Wireless Metropolitan Area Network (WMAN) links buildings within a metropolitan area, not a provisioned tablet across a region.
A Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) serves the hotspot, where any device joins without a provider subscription.
A Wireless Personal Area Network (WPAN) reaches about 10 meters around one person, far short of a region.
This type covers regions through cellular service providers, and handheld devices must be provisioned or subscribed.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush adds battery-powered thermostats and lighting sensors across a large warehouse. The sensors at the far end are too distant to reach the controller on their own, so their readings travel through the other sensors on the way. Each sensor sends only small readings, and the batteries must last for years. Which technology fits these sensors?

keywords.text: readings travel through the other sensors

answers.rationale: This protocol passes data through a mesh of intermediate devices and suits thermostats and long battery life.
Bluetooth is low power but links nearby devices directly; no relay through other devices is described.
Li-Fi uses light from Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) and cannot pass through the warehouse shelving.
WiMAX is long-range broadband for laptops and communities, not low-data battery sensors.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans a high-speed link for a crowded briefing room where many radio signals already cause interference. Security staff also require that the signal stay inside the room and never pass through the walls to the hallway. MSgt Rush warns that each adjoining room would then need transmitters of its own for an airman to keep coverage while walking between rooms. Which technology fits?

answers.rationale: Bluetooth uses radio waves near 2.45 Gigahertz (GHz), so it shares the crowded radio environment.
Wi-Fi uses radio frequencies that are prone to interference and pass beyond the room.
ZigBee is a low-rate 2.4 Gigahertz (GHz) radio protocol, neither high speed nor free of radio interference.
This technology has fewer interference issues than radio and cannot penetrate solid materials, so each area needs transmitters.

questions.stem: The Wireless LAN Controller (WLC) in a server room loses power during a storm. The Access Points (APs) on the office floor stay powered and still receive frames from the connected laptops, yet no frame reaches any destination, not even between two laptops on the same AP. Which type of AP is installed on the office floor?

answers.rationale: Autonomous Access Points (APs) contain their own controller and manage traffic without outside support.
These send every received frame to the controller, which decides whether to forward or discard it.
Multifunction Access Points (APs) act as switch and router too, so they forward frames themselves.
Rogue Access Points (APs) are unauthorized devices; nothing ties their forwarding to the server room controller.

questions.stem: On a walk-through of a squadron break room, MSgt Rush finds an inexpensive wireless router plugged into a wall jack on the secure network. An airman set it up so personal phones could get a signal there, meant no harm, and never asked the local network administrator. The box works as router, switch and wireless access device at once. Which type of Access Point (AP) has MSgt Rush found?

keywords.text: never asked the local network administrator

answers.rationale: Combining router, switch and wireless access describes the box, but the box was never authorized on the network.
Self-contained management describes many devices, but the box was never authorized on the network.
It was installed on a secure network without explicit authorization, maliciously or not, from a local administrator.
A Lightweight Access Point (LWAP) depends on a controller, and nothing in the break room is tied to one.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans a new copper run to a print room past generators and air conditioners. Twisting alone has not kept noise out of the old cable, and the new cable must still hold four twisted pairs. An airman warns that the conduit will fill quicker with the new cable. Which cable is MSgt Rush planning to install?

answers.rationale: Its added shielding cuts outside noise, and its thicker build fills a conduit quicker than other copper cable.
Twisting is its primary noise method, and it lacks the added layers that make a cable thicker.
This pin layout of thin copper cable joins like devices and adds no noise shielding.
This glass cable carries light and has no twisted copper pairs.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must link two sites several kilometers apart with one cable run buried under a road. Diode-fed fiber already serves the backbone inside each building, but its segments top out near 2000 meters. The new link also needs room to grow in bandwidth. Which medium should MSgt Rush order for the run?

answers.rationale: Its diode-fed segments reach about 2000 meters, short of a run several kilometers long.
Its single mode of laser light supports much longer segments and higher bandwidth than other guided media.
Copper twisted pair carries data up to about 100 meters, far short of this run.
This unguided method uses a laser beam through the air, not a buried cable.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's radio link was jammed often while it stayed on one known carrier. After a change, the link moves through a range of frequencies in a repeated pattern, and the jamming stops for several weeks. Then an attacker jams the link again. What did the attacker most likely work out to do this?

answers.text: The single carrier frequency in use
answers.rationale: The link no longer stays on one carrier, so knowing a single frequency does not let an attacker jam it.

answers.text: The alignment of the two devices
answers.rationale: Device alignment matters for laser links, not for radio signals that vary in frequency.

answers.text: The timing and pattern of the changes
answers.rationale: Once an attacker learns the timing and pattern of the frequency changes, the signal can be jammed.

answers.text: The routing of the buried cable
answers.rationale: A radio link sends its signal through the air, so no cable routing applies.

questions.stem: A new router sits on MSgt Rush's bench, and a computer must connect directly to the router so that MSgt Rush can make programming changes before the router joins the network. An airman offers to build the cable from a spool of twisted pair and two connectors. How should the airman wire the ends of this cable?

answers.text: Same standard on both ends, wired straight
answers.rationale: Matching pins without a flip form the cable that joins unlike devices, such as a computer and a switch.

answers.text: T-568A on one end, T-568B on the other
answers.rationale: One standard on each end swaps transmit and receive pins to join like devices.

answers.text: Two pair telephone plugs on both ends
answers.rationale: Two pair connectors serve common telephone service, not device programming.

answers.text: Same standard on both ends, cable flipped
answers.rationale: Programming a router from a computer uses the console cable, whose ends use one standard with the cable flipped.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush links two buildings across a flight line where no cable can be buried. During installation the two devices had to be precisely aligned. One afternoon an aircraft tug parks between the buildings, and the link drops until the tug drives away, although no storm or fog is present. Which medium is the link using?

answers.rationale: These radio signals ride one known carrier and are not described as needing a clear path.
Lasers send a focused beam that needs precise alignment and a clear line of sight between devices.
These radio signals vary across a broad band and are not described as needing a clear path.
This guided medium needs a cable run, and no cable can be buried here.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans a backbone between the floors of one large building. The longest run is about 400 meters, too far for twisted-pair cable. The budget rules out expensive lasers, so the equipment at each end must cost less than a laser link. Which medium fits this backbone?

answers.rationale: It uses expensive lasers as its light source, which the budget rules out.
Copper twisted pair carries data up to about 100 meters, short of this run.
Its diode-fed core supports longer segments than twisted pair, and its equipment costs less than the laser type.
This economical copper cable is limited to runs of about 100 meters.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush spends a shift restoring a switch that keeps dropping users. A module swap based on the top probable cause changes nothing; a configuration change written into the plan of action then clears the fault, and full system functionality checks out. As MSgt Rush closes the ticket, what should happen to the record of the failed module swap?

answers.text: Discard it once full functionality is verified
answers.rationale: Verifying functionality does not remove a failed attempt from the record of the work.

answers.text: List it among the plan's possible repercussions
answers.rationale: Repercussions are effects the fix may introduce, not attempts that already failed.

answers.text: Document it along with the working change
answers.rationale: Both positive and negative outcomes belong in the record so others avoid the same missteps.

answers.text: Return it to the list of probable causes
answers.rationale: The fault is already fixed, so the disproved theory is not ranked again.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush has confirmed that a failing module in a core switch is causing dropped calls. Replacing it will take phone service down in two buildings, so MSgt Rush notes that effect, coordinates with another office on a night window, and considers handing the job to a more senior level. Which troubleshooting step is MSgt Rush working in?

answers.rationale: This step identifies repercussions and downtime, schedules it with coordination, and may escalate.

answers.text: Test the theory to determine the cause
answers.rationale: The cause is already confirmed, so testing is finished, though escalation is also considered there.
Verification follows the executed fix, and the module has not been replaced yet.

answers.text: Establish a theory of probable cause
answers.rationale: Ranking probable causes comes before the cause is confirmed.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush connects a tone generator to one end of an unlabeled cable at an office wall jack, then carries the probe to a wiring closet to find the same cable in a large bundle. Loud cooling fans in the closet drown out any sound the probe makes. Which indication from the probe can still show MSgt Rush that it is nearing the right cable?

answers.rationale: A distance reading is given by a fiber reflection test, not by this probe.
The probe aids identification through intensified sounds or lights as it approaches the cable.
Pin arrangements are identified by a tester with both cable ends attached.
A numeric signal level is not an indication this probe is described as giving.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush tests a newly installed fiber optic run with an Optical Time Domain Reflectometer (OTDR). The run carries traffic and has no break, yet the test shows light reflected back from one point about halfway along the cable. Going by what the OTDR measures, which feature of the run most likely caused that reflection?

answers.rationale: Attenuation is detected by measuring signal strength with a meter, not by a reflection.
The test sends its own signal and needs no far-end source.
Electrical interference is not something light reflects off in fiber.
It measures light reflected off a break, splice, or defect in the fiber.

questions.stem: A fiber optic link between two buildings has no breaks, but traffic keeps dropping, and MSgt Rush suspects excessive attenuation. An optical light source is already attached at one end. MSgt Rush can only use the tools in the kit at the far end and must measure the strength of the arriving signal. Which tool from the kit does this job?

answers.rationale: It works with an optical light source to measure signal strength and detect excessive attenuation.
It lets a device test itself through one cable and does not measure fiber signal strength.
It measures voltage, resistance, and continuity in electrical circuits, not light.
It measures connection speed with sample files, not the strength of light.

questions.stem: During a security assessment, MSgt Rush must learn which services a remote server exposes, because an unexpected service may be running. MSgt Rush works from a workstation, cannot log in to the server, and needs neither packet contents nor connections on the workstation itself, only which virtual ports and services on that host are open. Which tool fits?

answers.rationale: It displays the local host's own active connections, not the services of a remote server.
It captures packets to read their contents, which the task excludes.
It identifies open virtual ports and services on a host for security assessments.
It shows cached address mappings for recent devices, not open services.

questions.stem: Airmen at a remote site report a slow web application at the main base. MSgt Rush plans to run tracert to see each router on the path, but a firewall between the sites drops traffic unless its message type is allowed. To get results, which messages must the firewall team allow tracert to send?

answers.text: Echo Requests with a fixed Time to Live (TTL) value
answers.rationale: A fixed value would not reveal each router along the route.

answers.text: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) probes with varying Time to Live (TTL) values
answers.rationale: These are not the messages tracert is described as sending.

answers.text: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) probes with varying Time to Live (TTL) values
answers.rationale: These are not the messages tracert is described as sending.

answers.text: Echo Requests with varying Time to Live (TTL) values
answers.rationale: It sends Echo Request messages with varying Time to Live (TTL) values to map each hop.

questions.stem: While reviewing a list of active connections, MSgt Rush finds a foreign Internet Protocol (IP) address that the workstation keeps contacting. MSgt Rush needs the domain name that belongs to that address, to help with a Domain Name System (DNS) related task. The address is all MSgt Rush has. Which command gives the domain name for it?

answers.rationale: It translates domain names to addresses and also addresses back to names.
It maps addresses of recently contacted devices to hardware addresses, not names.
It shows the local host's own settings and does not translate an address.
It displays active connections and states, which is where the address came from.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's Network Monitoring System (NMS) lists a new server on its discovered device list and has assigned it a device role. When the switch that serves the server fails, the NMS cannot show which devices lost their connection, because it never learned which switch the server plugs into. Which capability is this NMS missing?

answers.text: A drawing tool for the map
answers.rationale: A drawing tool relies on the administrator's knowledge, so the system still would not learn the connections.
The server already has an assigned device role, which defines what to watch, not how it connects.
Layer 2 or 3 discovery finds the port-to-port connectivity between devices on the network.
Historical data exposes trends but does not find how devices are connected.

questions.stem: To save energy costs, MSgt Rush's unit shuts its printers down every night. Each morning the Network Monitoring System (NMS) has sent dozens of overnight notices that the printers are down, burying real problems. MSgt Rush still wants a notice if a printer fails during the workday. Which alert setting fixes this?

answers.text: A blackout period for evening hours
answers.rationale: A blackout period suspends printer alerts during evening hours while the printers are shut down.

answers.text: A time element of ten minutes
answers.rationale: The printers stay down all night, far longer than a short time element, so the notices still go out.
Processor use does not matter when a printer is powered off, so the notices continue.

answers.text: A Syslog message for each event
answers.rationale: Syslog sends messages when an event affects a device, which adds notices rather than suspending them.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's Network Monitoring System (NMS) already checks ping availability, processor, memory, disk, and interface use on every device. Last week a fan failed inside a core switch and the wiring closet overheated, and neither problem showed up until the switch shut down. Which NMS function should MSgt Rush extend to check these items?

answers.rationale: Discovery finds devices and how they connect, not the condition of their parts.
Alerting notifies administrators after a check finds a problem; it does not add the checks.
Reporting provides real-time and historical data from the checks that already exist.
This function offers checks for fans, power supplies, and wiring closet temperature beyond the big 5.

questions.stem: On Monday the Network Monitoring System (NMS) stops receiving processor values from every router and switch at once. When MSgt Rush queries one switch directly from a laptop, its built-in Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) software answers normally, and so do the next ten devices tried. Which part inside the NMS most likely stopped working?

answers.rationale: The built-in software on the devices answers normally, so the problem is not on the devices.
Within the monitoring system, this component establishes communications with the agents and queries them.
This browser navigates stored objects to find more to watch; it does not carry the queries.
This tool watches traffic for attacks and does not collect processor values.

questions.stem: Late one night a workstation on MSgt Rush's network begins sending bursts of traffic unlike anything seen on it before. The pattern matches no signature of any known attack, yet the Intrusion Detection System (IDS) placed on the network still alerts the administrators. What lets the IDS recognize this activity?

answers.text: A match to a known signature
answers.rationale: The pattern matches no signature of any known attack, so a signature match is ruled out.

answers.text: A threshold with a time element
answers.rationale: Thresholds with a time element belong to monitoring system alerts, not attack detection.
An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) also works by looking for deviations from normal activity.
Port-to-port discovery shows how devices connect and does not detect attacks.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush explains that grounding diverts dangerous currents to earth and activates fuses and circuit breakers that shut down the circuit. Which function does this describe?

answers.rationale: That function stops transient surges from reaching damaging levels.
Diverting dangerous currents and tripping protective devices keeps people safe.
That function limits interference and power surges in signals.
Signal referencing sets a common voltage point and is not a grounding function.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush joins two metal surfaces with bolts, lock-washers, and clamps so the joint can be disassembled later. Which type of direct bond does this describe?

answers.rationale: A welded or brazed joint cannot be taken apart.
A strap is used when joining surfaces directly is not practical.
A signal reference bond is normally indirect, using crimps or connectors.
Bolts and clamps hold metal surfaces rigidly yet allow later disassembly.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds equipment that works correctly at times and not at others after an Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) event. Which cause explains this behavior?

answers.rationale: Minor damage makes components work sometimes and not other times.
Total destruction would stop operation completely.
A delayed breakdown follows a period of normal operation.
The pages do not link this behavior to a weak power supply.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds a component damaged by Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) that still seems to work. Which outcome is expected later in its life?

answers.rationale: Immediate melting would be visible at once.
Irregular operation shows up from the start.
The part seems normal but breaks down before its expected life span.
The pages say such damage shortens life span.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must shred classified documents. Which requirement applies to the classified burn or shred area, a No-Lone Zone, during this task?

answers.rationale: Two people must be in attendance while shredding classified documents.
A badge and a purpose apply to a different area type.
Identification applies to a different area type.
Approval before construction covers facility requirements, not this task.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reads that compliance with an Air Force Instruction (AFI) is mandatory. Failure to comply can result in action taken under which authority?

answers.rationale: A policy directive dictates policy for these instructions; it is not the authority for enforcement action.
This directorate hosts defense documents and does not take action on noncompliance.
This agency manages security implementation guides and does not enforce instruction compliance.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush traces the paths on an older desktop motherboard. A newly installed video graphics adapter and the added Random Access Memory (RAM) both exchange data with the Central Processing Unit (CPU) through one discrete chip, while the Universal Serial Bus (USB) ports and the disk drive controller go through another. Which part handles the adapter and memory traffic?

answers.rationale: This chip serves the low speed devices, such as the port and disk drive controllers.
This bus links the board to the slot the adapter sits in, not to the processor.
It is the high-speed interface between the processor, memory, and the video graphics adapter.
This is the set of address, control, and data buses, not a discrete chip.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush examines a workstation motherboard. The Universal Serial Bus (USB) controller and the Hard Disk Drive (HDD) controller both reach the Central Processing Unit (CPU) through a single chip labeled Fusion Controller Hub, separate from the path that serves memory and video. answers.rationale: This function serves the high speed devices, the memory and the video adapter.

This part makes the physical connection to external ports and handles no disk traffic.
This circuit controls the connected port devices only, not the disk drive controller.

questions.stem: While an application saves a large file, the Central Processing Unit (CPU) sends results out to main memory. answers.rationale: This manual governs software use and asset management, not secure settings.
This is an acquisition agreement, not a source of secure settings.

questions.stem: A new collaboration tool must be tested and certified at a Department of Defense (DoD) lab before it can appear on the Department of Defense Information Network (DoDIN) Approved Product List (APL) used by Military Departments. MSgt Rush wants to know which organization manages that approval process. Which one should MSgt Rush contact?

answers.rationale: This is the lead command for license management, not the list process.
This office of the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) manages the list process.
This office holds top software license authority, not the list process.
Network operations runs the network but does not manage product certification.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's unit asks to install a purchased commercial chart-making program on Air Force Network (AFNET) workstations. Before anyone installs it, MSgt Rush must confirm that the program has already been cleared for use on Air Force networks. Which resource should MSgt Rush consult?

answers.rationale: This list names all software approved for use on Air Force Network (AFNET) systems.
These guides set secure configuration for testing; they do not list cleared programs.
This is a way to acquire software, not a record of cleared programs.

answers.text: Department of the Air Force Manual (DAFMAN) 17-1203
answers.rationale: This manual governs software use but does not list approved programs.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must decide which guidance covers each of two software items for a unit inventory: a commercial office program the Air Force procured, and software integrated into an aircraft weapon system. Which publication covers the first item but not the second?

keywords.text: first item but not the second

answers.rationale: These guides set secure configuration for product testing, not coverage of procured software.
This list records approved software; it is not the governing publication.
This configuration applies to desktop software, not to the coverage split described.

answers.text: Department of the Air Force Manual (DAFMAN) 17-1203
answers.rationale: This manual applies to procured commercial software but not to software in a weapon system.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sorts two programs for a unit inventory. One was written under contract for a unique Air Force mission and exists nowhere else. The other is a packaged product that any business can buy and install into existing systems with no changes. Which term describes the second program?

answers.rationale: This is a purchase agreement for software or maintenance, not a kind of program.
This is a way to buy multiple copies, not a kind of program.
Ready-made products sold to the public and installed without customization fall in this category.
Drivers make hardware function; a packaged business product is not one.

questions.stem: A unit asks to load a free database app onto Air Force Network (AFNET) workstations. A failing database there could destroy valuable information across the whole network, so the app must first be vetted and tested. Which concern does that vetting address?

answers.text: Payment of a set enterprise price
answers.rationale: Pricing concerns acquisition of copies, not network vetting.

answers.text: Freedom from malware and security vulnerabilities
answers.rationale: Network applications are vetted and tested to be free of malware and security vulnerabilities.
Copyright is the author's legal right, not what vetting checks.

answers.text: Ability to run without system software
answers.rationale: Applications always need system software, and vetting does not test that.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares two workstations with the same processor family and the same amount of Random Access Memory (RAM). The faster one keeps more of its frequently used data in a three-level hierarchy of static memory right beside the processor, so it fetches from main memory less often. Which component difference best explains why that workstation is faster?

answers.rationale: Registers hold an instruction, address, or data for internal operations; they are not the three-level hierarchy described.
The control unit directs the processor with timing and control signals; it does not hold frequently used data.
The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs math on binary integers rather than keeping data near the processor.
Cache is a three-level hierarchy of static memory near the processor that cuts fetches from main memory.

questions.stem: An instruction arrives telling the Central Processing Unit (CPU) to add the contents of two defined registers and place the result in a third register. MSgt Rush asks an airman which part of the CPU actually carries out the addition of the two binary integers once both values are available. Which part performs that math?

answers.text: The registers named in the instruction
answers.rationale: Registers hold the values and the result, but they do not perform the math operation.

answers.text: The control unit that times the instruction
answers.rationale: The control unit directs the operation with timing and control signals rather than performing math.
Cache stores frequently accessed data to reduce fetch time; it does not perform the addition.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush traces one program instruction through a workstation. Data must move from the Central Processing Unit (CPU) to main memory and then out to a printer, and each of those devices must be told how to respond to the instruction. Which part of the CPU directs that flow of data and tells each device how to respond?

answers.rationale: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs math and logic operations; it does not tell devices how to respond.
The control unit directs the flow of data between the processor and other devices and tells them how to respond.
Registers hold an instruction, address, or data inside the processor; they do not direct other devices.
Processor cache holds frequently accessed data to cut fetch time; it does not direct other devices.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush prepares a 128 gigabyte Secure Digital (SD) card for a field camera that records single video files larger than 4 gigabytes. The card must follow the file system standard that the SD association adopted for cards of this size, and it must still work in most cameras, game consoles, and smartphones. Which file system should MSgt Rush choose?

answers.rationale: FAT32 works almost everywhere, but no individual file on it can be larger than 4 gigabytes.
New Technology File System (NTFS) handles large files but is not the standard adopted for these cards.
Extended File Allocation Table (exFAT) has no practical file size limit and is the adopted standard for cards of this size.
GUID Partition Table (GPT) is a disk partitioning system, so it cannot be the file system chosen.

questions.stem: An airman copies a 6 gigabyte training video onto a Universal Serial Bus (USB) flash drive that has 20 gigabytes free. The copy fails at once, although smaller files copy without trouble. The same drive works in almost every camera, smart television, and game console in the office. Which condition most likely explains the failed copy?

answers.text: The drive is formatted with Extended File Allocation Table (exFAT)
answers.rationale: Extended File Allocation Table (exFAT) has no practical file size limit, so a 6 gigabyte file would copy.

answers.text: The drive is formatted with FAT32
answers.rationale: FAT32 cannot hold a single file as large as this video, though FAT32 works with almost any device.

answers.text: The drive uses a Master Boot Record (MBR)
answers.rationale: Master Boot Record (MBR) limits partitions to two terabytes combined, far above this drive's size.

answers.text: The drive has New Technology File System (NTFS) quotas
answers.rationale: Quotas limit each account's share of disk space, but nothing shows a quota on this portable drive.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush installs a new 3 terabyte drive in an older workstation and divides it with a legacy partitioning scheme. Disk Management shows the drive working, but only 2 terabytes of space can ever be allocated, and a fifth primary partition cannot be created. Which partitioning system was used on the drive?

answers.rationale: Master Boot Record (MBR) allows only a few primary partitions per disk, and all partitions combined cannot exceed two terabytes.
GUID Partition Table (GPT) overcomes the two terabyte limit and allows a vast number of partitions.
New Technology File System (NTFS) is a file system, and it supports partitions far larger than this drive.
FAT32 is a file system whose partitions can reach 8 terabytes, so it is not a partitioning scheme.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush wants to divide a 12 terabyte drive into many partitions in an older workstation. Its motherboard supports legacy Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) startup with no Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) option at all. Which partitioning system is ruled out on this workstation by the motherboard itself?

answers.rationale: Master Boot Record (MBR) works with legacy startup, though it limits the disk to two terabytes.
GUID Partition Table (GPT) is part of the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) specification, so it needs UEFI enabled.

answers.text: Logical partitions in an extended partition
answers.rationale: Logical partitions inside an extended partition belong to the legacy scheme, which this motherboard supports.

answers.text: Primary partitions with a partition table
answers.rationale: Primary partitions described by a partition table belong to the legacy scheme that this motherboard supports.

questions.stem: A storm cuts power to MSgt Rush's Windows workstation while several documents are being saved to its New Technology File System (NTFS) partition. After the restart, the file system replays its record of the pending file changes, and the documents are recovered intact. Which NTFS feature made that recovery possible?

answers.rationale: Bad sector mapping keeps Windows from using damaged sectors; it does not record pending file changes.
Compression shrinks files to save disk space and may slow processing; it does not recover files.
Journaling keeps a running record of file changes so files can be recovered after a power failure.
Permissions control which accounts can reach which files; they do not recover interrupted saves.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush manages a shared Windows file server where twenty airmen save work to one New Technology File System (NTFS) volume. Each airman can already open only the right folders, yet one airman's video archive keeps filling the volume until others cannot save anything. Which NTFS feature should MSgt Rush configure to stop this from happening again?

answers.rationale: Permissions already control which folders each airman can open; they do not cap the space used.
Compression saves some space, but it puts no limit on how much one airman can store.
Partition resizing could add space once, but one archive could still fill the larger volume.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must pick a medium for yearly enterprise network backups that will sit on a shelf for many years and may be bumped during transport. Months later, restoring one file stored near the end of a large backup takes a long time, because all the data recorded before it must pass under the read head first. Which medium did MSgt Rush pick?

answers.rationale: A Solid State Drive (SSD) resists shock but offers faster access, not slow sequential reading.
A Blu-ray Disc (BD) is optical media read by a laser, not data passing under a read head.
Magnetic tape resists shock, keeps data for a long shelf-life, and stores data in sequential format.
A Hard Disk Drive (HDD) is easily harmed by drops and physical shock, which can cause a head crash.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush has one spare drive to share between a server with a Serial Attached SCSI (SAS) bus and a desktop whose motherboard offers only a Serial ATA (SATA) interface. The spare must work in either machine and should not need any hardware jumper settings. Which drive standard should the spare use?

answers.rationale: Parallel ATA (PATA) is a legacy standard with ribbon cables and hardware jumpers for configuration.
A Serial Attached SCSI (SAS) drive cannot interface with the desktop's serial interface.
Universal Serial Bus (USB) is a port standard rather than an internal drive interface here.
A Serial ATA (SATA) drive is compatible with the server bus, and most need no jumper configuration.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds an unlabeled optical disc that fits the same tray as a Compact Disc (CD). The drive reads it with a 650 nanometer red laser, and the disc holds far more than a CD because its pits and lands are smaller and packed closer together. Which type of disc has MSgt Rush found?

answers.rationale: A Blu-ray Disc (BD) also fits the tray, but it is read with a 405 nanometer blue-violet laser.
A Digital Versatile Disc (DVD) is read with a 650 nanometer red laser and has smaller, tighter pits.
A Compact Disc-Rewriteable (CD-RW) extends Compact Disc (CD) technology and holds no more than a CD.
A Compact Disc (CD) is read with a 780 nanometer laser and holds about 700 megabytes.

questions.stem: An airman installs a second, brand-new Hard Disk Drive (HDD) in a Windows workstation. The drive spins up and appears in the Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) settings, yet Windows shows no drive letter for it and cannot store anything on it. Which step must happen first to make the new drive visible to the Operating System (OS)?

answers.text: Formatting it with a file system
answers.rationale: Formatting with a file system comes after the drive is divided, so it cannot be the first step.
Journaling is a file system feature, which needs a formatted partition before it can work.
Partitioning is the first step; it divides the drive and makes it visible to the Operating System (OS).
Resizing the existing system partition changes another drive and does not prepare the new one.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush watches a workstation start. Before the desktop appears, one part of the Operating System (OS) loads and begins deciding which running programs get processing time and how memory is shared. Later, an airman opens folders that keep user files apart from system files. Which part loaded first and handles that sharing of processing time and memory?

answers.rationale: The file system keeps user files apart from system files but does not manage resources.
The desktop interface appears after startup and hides complexity; it does not allocate resources.
The kernel loads first and manages processor time and memory for running programs.
Program execution gives applications a compatible environment; it does not load first.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush updates the display drivers on a workstation every few months. The small programs stored on a chip on the motherboard, which show a video display while the computer boots, have not changed in years. Which kind of software are those small programs on the chip?

answers.rationale: Firmware is small programs on a chip, seldom updated, that give a display during boot.
The kernel is the core of the system that loads after boot and holds many drivers.
The chip itself is hardware, but the programs stored on it are software.
The system software is regularly updated, unlike these small programs.

questions.stem: When a workstation powers on, one program offers a menu to set boot priority and system time, guards those settings with a password, and loads basic device drivers. Once the computer can boot, a second program runs the desktop and applications. Why does the first program not count as an Operating System (OS)?

answers.text: It provides no drivers or system security
answers.rationale: The program shows drivers, a menu and password security, so that is not the reason.

answers.text: It is stored as files on a Hard Disk Drive (HDD)
answers.rationale: It is firmware on a chip, not files on a disk drive.

answers.text: It is closed-source code locked by a license
answers.rationale: Licensing is not the stated reason; the reason concerns what the program is for.

answers.text: It exists to turn the computer over at boot
answers.rationale: Its purpose is to turn the computer over to the system as soon as it can boot.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must run an original Microsoft Disk Operating System (MSDOS) text command for maintenance on a Windows 11 workstation, which no longer depends on MSDOS. CMD is locked by local policy, so MSgt Rush needs another Windows command prompt that still offers those commands. Which tool should MSgt Rush open?

answers.rationale: A Linux terminal gives a command prompt on Linux systems, not on Windows.
PowerShell, like CMD, still offers many original text commands on Windows.
The desktop interface uses mouse and touch; it is not a command prompt.
The kernel is the core of Windows, not a prompt for typed commands.

questions.stem: An airman compares two workstations. One runs an early Windows release that was a graphical shell hiding an older system's command prompt. The other runs Windows 11, which still offers many of that older system's text commands through CMD but no longer depends on that system. What is Windows 11 based on that removed the dependence?

answers.rationale: Every modern version is based on the New Technology (NT) kernel.
Darwin XNU underlies the Apple iOS system, not Windows.
Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) firmware only wakes the computer at boot.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds a flaw in a Windows component and wants to read its source code and change it to fit the needs of the unit. Windows is proprietary and comes with restrictive licensing. What makes even viewing that code illegal for MSgt Rush?

answers.rationale: The Standard Desktop Configuration (SDC) is a Windows desktop baseline, not a legal agreement.
A walled garden is the Apple iPhone app store model.
Freeware licenses, such as the Chrome license, allow free use rather than forbid it.
Legally binding End-User License Agreements (EULA) make modifying or viewing Windows code illegal.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush needs a system for a lab router that the unit can change to suit one purpose, without expensive licensing. The options are a compact Windows edition, MacOS, and a popular UNIX version. Which property of the UNIX version makes it the fit?

answers.text: Its code is free and open source
answers.rationale: Popular UNIX versions are free and open source, so anyone may modify them.
Windows is closed source and illegal to modify, so that property does not fit.

answers.text: Its kernel alone is open source
answers.rationale: An open kernel with closed desktop tools describes MacOS, not popular UNIX versions.
Closed code with some open parts describes iOS, not popular UNIX versions.

questions.stem: An airman reads that the system on a Macintosh laptop is based on UNIX and borrows features from two projects. One is an open-source version of UNIX that another group created; Apple itself developed the other. MSgt Rush asks the airman to name the project that Apple developed. Which project is it?

answers.rationale: FreeBSD is the open-source UNIX version, not the project Apple developed.
AT&T UNIX came from Bell Labs Research Center, not from Apple.
MacOS borrows features from Darwin, which Apple developed.
Linux came from Linus Torvalds and is not named as a MacOS source.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush tells an airman that the Android tablets, Chromebook laptops, and Ubuntu servers of the unit share one free, open-source piece that a Finnish programmer created in 1991. By itself, that piece is not a complete system. Which piece do the devices share?

answers.rationale: Android, ChromeOS and Ubuntu are built on the Linux kernel, created in 1991.
AT&T UNIX dates from the 1970s at Bell Labs and is a family of complete systems.
Darwin XNU is the Apple kernel under iOS.
FreeBSD is an open-source UNIX version that MacOS borrows from, not these devices.

questions.stem: An airman is issued a laptop whose system keeps user data and applications in the cloud, includes a media player among its few built-in apps, and can run Android apps from the official store. Which system runs on the laptop?

answers.rationale: Android is a mobile touch-screen system, not described as cloud based.
Linux is the kernel that system builds on, not itself a full system.
ChromeOS keeps data and apps in the cloud and can run Android apps.
MacOS is the Apple desktop system and is not described as cloud based.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is choosing a system for unit tablets. The tablets must accept an individual app installed directly by an airman, outside any official store, and the tablet vendor wants to print the name of the system on the box. Which system fits, and what must the vendor do?

answers.text: iOS, after joining the App Store
answers.rationale: iOS is a walled garden that blocks user-directed installations.
Certification for the official store is not the trademark step vendors need.
iPadOS is based on iOS and keeps its closed app model.
Android allows sideloading, and vendors must license the trademarked name from Google.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's unit already ranks its cybersecurity risks by potential impact. It now wants McAfee capabilities on its devices that stop malware and filter traffic with a firewall, while the unit keeps running the service itself instead of handing control to McAfee. Which McAfee offering fits?

answers.rationale: Ranking risks by impact is what the unit already does with that service.
That offering is fully managed, with McAfee deploying and controlling it.
The antivirus application alone is not described with firewall capabilities.

questions.stem: An airman tries to add an app to a unit iPhone from a third-party store found online, a step that is easy on Android devices. The installation is refused. MSgt Rush explains the business model Apple uses that causes the refusal. What is the model called?

answers.rationale: Sideloading is the Android process of adding unofficial apps.
Closed source describes iOS code, not the app store business model.
Freeware licensing lets software be used at no cost; it does not block stores.
The Apple walled garden restricts third-party stores and user-directed installations.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sets up a certified Chromebook and a certified Android phone for an airman. MSgt Rush wants both devices to get apps that are screened for security from their official source rather than from an outside store. Which source should MSgt Rush use for both?

answers.rationale: Google Play Store is the official, screened source for certified Android and ChromeOS devices.
The Apple App Store serves iPhone apps only.
An outside store means sideloading, which raises security concerns.
Chromium is an open-source browser project, not an app source.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush needs one Microsoft Office application to keep the meeting schedule of an airman, store contact details for the flight, and send email to those contacts. Meeting notes will be kept in a different program. Which application handles all three needs?

answers.rationale: OneNote is the note taking program, the place for the meeting notes.
Outlook is the calendar, address book and email client.
Skype for Business hosts real-time conferences, not a calendar and address book.
Teams is for chat, meetings, notes and attachments, not an address book and email.

questions.stem: An Air Force squadron wants one web-based collaborative platform that integrates with Microsoft Office, where members of its committees and additional duties can store and manage their documents. Chat and live meetings are already handled by another program. Which application fits the need?

answers.rationale: Teams is the workplace platform for chat, meetings, notes and attachments.
Office 365 is the subscription service that delivers the Office suite.
SharePoint is a web-based collaborative platform, primarily for document management and storage.
OneNote is the note taking program, not a document management platform.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares two browsers on a workstation. One comes bundled with Windows and replaced an older Microsoft browser; the other is the freeware browser from Google with a more polished interface. Both are built on the same free, open-source foundation. Which foundation do they share?

answers.rationale: Chrome is the Google browser itself, built on top of that foundation.
Internet Explorer (IE) is the older browser that Edge replaced.
Edge and Chrome are both built on the open-source Chromium browser.
ChromeOS is a Google system, not a browser foundation.

questions.stem: A squadron lobby workstation must let visitors fill in one sign-in page without typing any name or password. Last month, visitors who used the shared visitor account also browsed websites and checked email on it. MSgt Rush must stop that while keeping the sign-in page open to anyone who walks up. Which account should MSgt Rush set up?

answers.rationale: This special account needs no logon credentials and allows just one application, such as a sign-in page.
Guest users can still browse the web and check email, which must stop.
A Standard account is password protected and opens most of the computer.
This is a Standard account with Family Safety, so it still allows other applications.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush prepares a standalone Windows 10 laptop for a field site with no network connection. The laptop still needs an Administrator account and Standard accounts, and nobody will need paid apps, settings sync, or cloud storage. Which way of setting up Windows 10 fits this laptop?

answers.rationale: This setup brings sync, paid apps and cloud storage, which this laptop does not need.
Guest is an account created after setup; it is not a way of setting up Windows.
Kiosk is a one-application account created after setup, not a way of setting up Windows.
This setup needs no network connection and can still hold Administrator and Standard accounts.

questions.stem: On a workstation, MSgt Rush notices a program that quietly copies files and opens outside connections. A basic antivirus scan reports the computer clean, because nothing on it matches any entry in the database of known viruses. Which antivirus capability gives MSgt Rush the best chance of flagging this program?

answers.rationale: Definition matching already failed because the program matches no known virus entry.
This method looks for suspicious or malicious activity, so it can flag unknown malware.
Quarantine isolates a file after detection, and nothing has been detected yet.
Automatic scanning changes when a basic scan runs, not what the scan compares against.

questions.stem: An automatic scan reacts the moment an airman mounts portable media on a workstation: one file on the media matches an entry in the definitions database. MSgt Rush wants that file kept apart where it cannot run, rather than deleted, so that it can be examined later. Which antivirus action fits?

answers.rationale: Isolating the suspicious file instead of removing it is this action.
Heuristics is a way to detect malware, and the file is already detected.
A manual scan would check the file again; it does not set the file apart.
Updating definitions adds new threats to the database; it does not set a file apart.

questions.stem: A basic antivirus program on a squadron workstation catches older known viruses well, but it missed a virus released two days ago. MSgt Rush learns that the binary pattern for that virus is now available from the antivirus vendor. Updating which part of the antivirus database would let the basic scan catch that virus?

answers.rationale: Heuristics looks at behavior and is not what a basic scan compares files against.
The quarantine holds files already isolated; it does not identify new viruses.
A firewall rule set filters network packets and is not part of the antivirus database.
Basic scans compare files with these patterns, so the new pattern must be added to them.

questions.stem: An airman has three laptops, a desktop, and a printer at home, all connected to one residential router. The airman wants one layer of protection that monitors traffic between all of these devices and the public Internet, without installing anything on each laptop. Which protection fits?

answers.rationale: A software firewall is installed on each computer, which the airman wants to avoid.
This antivirus program runs on each computer; it does not filter router traffic.
A firewall on a residential router protects every device connected to it.
Heuristics is an antivirus detection method, not a traffic filter for the network.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds that one workstation lets a game application connect out through a port that the rule set forbids. Other workstations behind the same gateway block that game, and the gateway rules are correct. Which protection on the misbehaving workstation should MSgt Rush check?

answers.rationale: The gateway rules are correct and the other workstations behave, so the gateway is fine.
This firewall runs on each computer and monitors ports and applications against the rule set.
Quarantine isolates files that match virus definitions; it does not block connections.
Update policy keeps patches current; it does not block application connections.

questions.stem: During an inspection, MSgt Rush finds a client that has gone months without any security patches, and the network now refuses its connection. The client's account types and passwords are all in order. What must happen to the client before the network will accept it again?

answers.rationale: The passwords are already in order, and password rules do not restore network access.
Quarantine isolates a suspicious file; it does not bring a client back onto the network.

answers.text: It gets a Kiosk Mode account
answers.rationale: A Kiosk account limits a user to one application; it does not restore network access.
A client too far behind on security updates may be denied access until it can be re-imaged.

questions.stem: A squadron bought a volume purchase agreement for a design program. During an audit, MSgt Rush finds that the squadron reported fewer installations than the number of workstations actually running the program. Each copy came from the vendor's own media, the subscription is current, and nothing was downloaded from outside sites. Which type of piracy has occurred?

answers.rationale: Nothing came from outside sites, so no copies or keys were offered for download.
Under-reporting installations bought through a volume purchase agreement is this type of piracy.
The subscription is current, so its date has not passed.
The copies came from the vendor's own media, so nothing imitates original packaging.

questions.stem: An airman's office paid for one year of use of a mapping program. The year ended in March, nobody renewed, and the same legitimate copies kept running on the same number of licensed workstations. MSgt Rush notices this during a July inventory. Which type of piracy has the office committed?

answers.rationale: The office ran no more copies than it had licensed and reported nothing short.
The copies are legitimate, so nothing was made to look like an original.
Nothing was offered or downloaded, so no copies were provided to others.
Using licensed software past its subscription date is this type of piracy.

questions.stem: While checking a report, MSgt Rush finds a website that offers downloads of a popular office program together with serial numbers that unlock it. The site is not an authorized reseller, it ships no boxes or printed packaging, and no base workstation runs more copies than licensed. Which type of piracy is the website committing?

answers.rationale: A provider that is not an authorized reseller offering downloads and serial numbers commits this type.
No packaging is made to look like an original, so the product is not imitated.
No base workstation runs extra copies, so no organization under-reports or over-installs.
No subscription date has passed; the issue is who offers the copies.

questions.stem: A unit receives a boxed program from an unfamiliar seller. The disc, the box, and the printed manual look exactly like the vendor's, but the vendor confirms it never produced that box. The unit has not installed the program anywhere yet, and the seller offers no downloads or keys online. Which type of piracy has the seller committed?

answers.rationale: The seller offers no downloads or keys online, so nothing is provided over the internet.
Nothing was installed or used past a subscription date.
Copying the product and its packaging so it looks like an original is this type of piracy.
The unit has installed nothing, so it has not exceeded or under-reported licenses.

questions.stem: While traveling on Government business, MSgt Rush learns that a canceled flight moves the return trip one day later. From a government laptop, MSgt Rush sends a brief email telling family members about the new travel schedule. Under the Joint Ethics Regulation (JER), which category covers this message?

answers.rationale: This category covers emergencies and messages the government needs, not family schedule notes.
Brief messages to family about official transportation or schedule changes while traveling fit this category.
Morale and welfare use applies to members deployed for extended periods with theater commander approval.
A delayed return trip is not an emergency communication.

questions.stem: An organization buys laptops in bulk, each arriving with a licensed version of Windows preinstalled. MSgt Rush must bring them to the corporate standard and onto the network, but the remote sites they ship to have too few IT staff for hands-on work. The vendor can register the machines in advance, and the organization will pay a subscription. Which deployment method fits?

answers.rationale: Cloning needs hands-on drive work on identical hardware, which the remote sites cannot staff.
Network boot uses a local server and nothing is said about machines registered in advance.
This paid service remotely re-images preregistered new computers the first time they connect to a network.
A clean install on each laptop is the most time and labor intensive method.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must set up several workstations of the same make and model with the same applications, desktop layout, and configuration settings already on a finished parent workstation. Nothing should need to be reinstalled by hand, and the workstations have no network connection to any server. Which deployment method fits?

answers.rationale: This method copies Windows, settings, layout, files and applications onto identical hardware.
A clean install starts each computer from removable media, so applications must be reinstalled.
Network boot depends on a remote server, which these workstations cannot reach.
Autopilot re-images over a network connection, which these workstations do not have.

questions.stem: A small office has two computers and no server, no cloud subscription, and no spare hard drive to copy onto. MSgt Rush has a purchased Windows installation disc and will work on-premises at each computer. Which deployment method fits this office?

answers.rationale: Cloning needs a parent drive copied onto another drive, and no spare drive exists.

questions.stem: An airman unboxes a blank switch for a new office. No Internet Protocol (IP) address has been assigned yet, so the switch cannot accept a remote Telnet session over its ports. The address table lists learned devices and interfaces; it holds no configuration.

questions.stem: An airman sets up a dedicated link that connects exactly two network devices, one on each end, with no host or networking system between them.
