Reliability, load and Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) may also be used beyond the defaults.

questions.stem: An airman's host wrongly treats a server on another Local Area Network (LAN) as local and broadcasts an Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) request for it. The router between the two LANs answers on the server's behalf. Later, MSgt Rush views the host's ARP cache. Which address is stored there for the server's Internet Protocol (IP) address?

answers.rationale: The server never replies; the router answers in its place.
The router replies with its own physical address, which the host saves for the server.
Broadcasts carry the request; the reply stored in the cache is a single device address.
The logical address is what the host already knew; the cache maps it to another address.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush watches a newly powered router announce itself with Hello messages, and connected routers return Hello replies. Long after all its neighbors are known, the router still sends the same messages at specific intervals. What purpose do these later messages serve?

answers.text: A keep-alive that a neighbor still works
answers.rationale: Hello messages at specific intervals act as a keep-alive for connected routers.

answers.text: A full routing table for each neighbor
answers.rationale: Sending whole routing tables is a broadcast routing update, not this message.

answers.text: An error report back to each source
answers.rationale: Reporting errors back to the source is the job of Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP).

answers.text: A request for each neighbor's address mapping
answers.rationale: Mapping network addresses to physical addresses is done by Address Resolution Protocol (ARP).

questions.stem: An airman's host sends packets to a server, and a router along the way cannot forward them. The host then receives a Destination Unreachable message from the router. MSgt Rush notes that the routers forwarding the packets do not monitor delivery themselves. Which protocol carried that message back to the host?

answers.rationale: Internet Protocol (IP) does not report errors back to the source when routing anomalies occur.
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) maps addresses; it does not report delivery errors.
Hello Protocol discovers neighbors and acts as a keep-alive between devices.
This protocol reports errors about packet processing, including Destination Unreachable.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush tests a server that an airman cannot open a web application on. From the router, MSgt Rush sends a test to the server's Internet Protocol (IP) address and receives four echo replies with no loss. The web application still fails. What does the successful test show?

answers.text: The whole protocol stack is working
answers.rationale: The test does not check the entire protocol stack.

answers.text: The Network Layer path is working
answers.rationale: This is a Network Layer to Network Layer test through the network.
The echo reply comes from the Network Layer, not from the application.

answers.text: The Data Link Layer is failing
answers.rationale: Replies came back, so the lower layers carried the test successfully.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reviews a routing algorithm on a large base network. Instead of relying on one value, the algorithm weighs delay, bandwidth and load for every path at the same time and folds them into one number before it picks the best route to a destination network. What does such a sophisticated algorithm base its route selection on?

answers.rationale: Balanced hybrid names a protocol type that mixes two algorithm types, not combined metrics.
Sophisticated algorithms can combine multiple metrics in a single hybrid metric.
Path attributes are set by administrators for exterior routing, not folded from delay and load.
The pages give no composite distance; combined metrics form one hybrid value.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's routing protocol lets the administrators give each network link an arbitrary cost. When a packet's route crosses four links, the protocol adds the costs of those four links together and treats the total as the measure of that route. Which routing metric is MSgt Rush's protocol using to compare routes?

answers.rationale: Reliability ratings describe link dependability; they are not a sum along the route.
Communication cost concerns operating expenses of lines, not the sum of assigned link costs.
Path length is the sum of the costs associated with each link traversed.
Load measures how busy a resource is, such as processor use.

questions.stem: An airman notices that one network link goes down more often than the others and takes longer to repair after each failure. MSgt Rush says the routing algorithm can account for this through the link's reliability rating. How is that reliability rating usually produced?

answers.text: Assigned to links by network administrators
answers.rationale: Reliability ratings are arbitrary numeric values usually assigned to network links by network administrators.

answers.text: Measured as processor use on each router
answers.rationale: Processor use is one way to calculate load, a different metric.

answers.text: Reference bandwidth divided by link bandwidth
answers.rationale: Dividing a reference bandwidth gives the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) cost.

answers.text: Summed from the cost of each link crossed
answers.rationale: Summing link costs gives path length, not a reliability rating.

questions.stem: Packets between two of MSgt Rush's sites wait in port queues at each router along the way, cross congested intermediate links, and travel a long physical distance. MSgt Rush wants one routing metric that already depends on all of these factors together. Which metric is a conglomeration of these variables?

answers.rationale: Load is how busy a resource such as a router is, measured by processor use.
Bandwidth is only the available capacity of a link, one factor among several.
Path length sums link costs or counts hops, not queues and distance.
Delay depends on link bandwidth, port queues, congestion and physical distance, a conglomeration of variables.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush wants the routing algorithm to favor routers that are less busy, so it would track Central Processing Unit (CPU) utilization and packets processed per second on every router without a pause. Before choosing this metric, MSgt Rush checks the pages for a drawback. Which drawback of this metric do the pages point out?

answers.text: A faster busy link can take longer to send
answers.rationale: A busier fast link taking longer is the caution given for bandwidth.

answers.text: Monitoring it constantly uses many resources
answers.rationale: Monitoring load parameters on a continual basis can be resource intensive.

answers.text: Its ratings are arbitrary values set by hand
answers.rationale: Arbitrary values assigned by administrators describe reliability ratings.

answers.text: Faster links can round to the same cost
answers.rationale: Rounding faster links to equal cost is the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) cost issue.

questions.stem: A link fails on MSgt Rush's network, which runs Routing Information Protocol (RIP). The router next to the failure updates its routing table right away. MSgt Rush wants to know how news of the change then reaches routers several hops away, and why convergence takes longer than with other protocols. Which description matches the pages?

answers.text: Sent at once, one neighbor router at a time
answers.rationale: Updates go immediately, only to directly connected neighbors, one router at a time, so convergence takes longer.

answers.text: Held until the next scheduled 30-second update
answers.rationale: Change updates are sent independently of the regularly scheduled updates, not held for them.

answers.text: Multicast at once to routers throughout the area
answers.rationale: Multicast to the whole area describes Link State updates.

answers.text: Sent to neighbors that the administrator defined
answers.rationale: Manually defined neighbors describe Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), not this protocol.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush upgrades the routers from the original Routing Information Protocol (RIP) to version 2. Besides carrying subnet mask data in every routing update, the new version changes the way those updates are sent across the network, and the pages say this change speeds up convergence. Which change in sending updates is it?

answers.text: Updates are sent just on topology change
answers.rationale: Sending only on topology change describes Link State and Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) updates.

answers.text: Updates are acknowledged in a reliable session
answers.rationale: Acknowledged sessions describe Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) messaging.

answers.text: Updates are sent as multicast messages
answers.rationale: Version 2 uses multicast messages to send routing updates, which speeds up convergence time.

answers.text: Updates go to directly connected neighbors alone
answers.rationale: Sending only to directly connected neighbors is the original behavior that lengthens convergence.

questions.stem: A link on one router in MSgt Rush's Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) area goes down. Routers in the area learn of the change through Link State Advertisements (LSA), copy the information for their own use, and resend it through their other interfaces. Which routers generate the message about the change in the first place?

answers.rationale: Other routers in the area copy and resend the message; they do not generate it.
Area border routers join areas; they are not named as the routers that generate it.
Backbone routers distribute routes between areas; they do not originate this message.
Only the directly affected routers generate the message, so receivers know the information is valid.

questions.stem: Two routers in the same Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) area hold identical topology tables. An airman assumes they must therefore calculate the very same shortest path tree. MSgt Rush corrects the airman by explaining how Dijkstra's Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm builds the tree from the topology table on each router. What is the root of each router's tree?

answers.rationale: Area border routers link areas; the pages do not make them the root.
Each router calculates a shortest path tree with itself as the root.
The backbone distributes routes between areas; it is not the root of the tree.

answers.text: The router with the lowest cost
answers.rationale: Lowest cost picks paths along the tree; it does not choose the root.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush adds a 1 Gigabit link to an Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) network that still runs on default settings. The routers treat the new link as having the same cost as an older 100 Mbps link, so they do not favor the faster path. Which change do the pages give to solve this problem?

answers.rationale: Changing the bandwidth reference keeps faster links from appearing as the same cost as slower links.
Administrative Distance ranks routing sources; it does not change how link cost is figured.
Hold time sets how long a neighbor is treated as reachable.
A hop count limit belongs to Routing Information Protocol (RIP), not this cost problem.

questions.stem: In MSgt Rush's multi-area Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) network, area border routers connect areas 1 and 3 to area 0. An airman working on an intra-area router in area 1 expects to find the layout of area 0 in that router's topology table. What do the pages say about the backbone topology?

answers.text: It is identical in each router's table
answers.rationale: Identical topology tables hold only within one area, not across the whole network.

answers.text: It is stored just in neighbor tables
answers.rationale: Neighbor tables hold neighbor addresses and interfaces, not the backbone topology.

answers.text: It is invisible to intra-area routers
answers.rationale: The backbone topology is invisible to all intra-area routers, as area topologies are to the backbone.

answers.text: It is flooded into each area as updates
answers.rationale: Area topologies are kept separate, so the backbone layout is not flooded into areas.

questions.stem: An Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) router records a new neighbor's address and interface in its neighbor table. The neighbor's hello packets advertise a hold time. Later the hello packets from that neighbor stop arriving, and the hold time runs out with none received. What happens next on MSgt Rush's router?

answers.text: The administrator defines the neighbor again by hand
answers.rationale: Manually defined neighbors belong to Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), not this protocol.

answers.text: The router waits for the next scheduled update
answers.rationale: This protocol sends no periodic updates; it reacts when the network changes.

answers.text: The router sends its whole table to its neighbors
answers.rationale: Sending whole tables to neighbors describes Distance Vector algorithms.

answers.text: The routing algorithm is told of a topology change
answers.rationale: When the hold time expires, the Diffusing Update Algorithm (DUAL) is informed of the topology change.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) topology table lists three paths to one destination network, each learned from a different neighbor. The router works out a best route and a backup route among those three paths. Which of the paths does MSgt Rush's router advertise to its own neighbors?

answers.text: The successor and the feasible successor
answers.rationale: The backup route is kept in the topology table, not advertised.
The router advertises a route only if it forwards packets with it, the best route or successor.

answers.text: Every path in the topology table
answers.rationale: The topology table may hold other paths, but they are not advertised.
The backup route enters the routing table only if the best route fails.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) with other protocols for a growing network. The pages list fast convergence as an EIGRP advantage, but only under one condition. The best route to a network then fails on one of MSgt Rush's routers. Which condition decides whether that router converges fast?

answers.rationale: The protocol has no area concept, so a backbone area is not the condition.

answers.text: The hold time has not expired
answers.rationale: An expired hold time signals a change; it is not the convergence condition.
The listed advantage is fast convergence when a feasible successor is available.
Broadcast updates are tied to slower Distance Vector convergence.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reviews an upgrade plan for one layer of a three-layer network. The plan selects routing protocols with lower convergence times, adds FastEthernet with redundant links, and upgrades the existing routers instead of adding more routers as the internetwork grows. The devices of this layer also hand off traffic toward the outside world. Which layer is the plan written for?

answers.rationale: The distribution layer redistributes between routing protocols; the guidance on convergence times and avoiding expansion is written for another layer.
The access layer uses switches with many ports and low cost to connect desktops, not redundant high-speed links.
Core design selects routing protocols with lower convergence times, redundant media such as FastEthernet, and upgrades over expansion.
The physical layer belongs to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model, not to the three-layer hierarchical model.

questions.stem: File requests from one building to a server at a distant base are slow, while requests to the printers and certain servers inside the building stay fast. MSgt Rush must examine the layer that handles all traffic for remote services and determines the fastest way each request is serviced before the request is handed on for transport. Which layer does MSgt Rush examine?

answers.rationale: All traffic for remote services is handled by the distribution layer, which determines the best path and then forwards requests.
The core only transports traffic after another layer has determined the best path and forwarded the request.
The transport layer belongs to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model, not to the three-layer hierarchical model.
The access layer delivers frames to end user computers and holds the local printers and servers that stay fast.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush installs hubs that share bandwidth among several workstations in a building, sets Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership on the switch ports, and places a printer and certain servers that most airmen there need so they are available locally. The design guidance describes this layer as an aggregation point. Which layer of the three-layer model holds these devices?

answers.rationale: The core does not support workgroup access by connecting devices that belong to another layer.
The distribution layer routes between Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) and aggregates access switches, but does not hold shared bandwidth hubs for workstations.
The session layer belongs to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model, not to the three-layer hierarchical model.
Access switches include shared bandwidth devices and Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership, keep resources local, and form an aggregation point.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush breaks one subnet of a network into two further subnets while the other subnets keep their size, so the network now carries more than one subnet mask. The routers still run Routing Information Protocol (RIP) version 1. One router receives a packet for one of the new smaller subnets, and that router has a subnet of the same network number on its local interface. Which mask does the router assume for the packet?

answers.text: A classful mask for the address
answers.rationale: A classful mask is assumed only when the router has no subnet of the same network number on a local interface.

answers.text: The same mask as its local interface
answers.rationale: With a subnet of the same network number locally, a version 1 router assumes the incoming packet uses that interface's mask.

answers.text: The mask value sent in route advertisements
answers.rationale: Newer protocols such as Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) send the mask value with route advertisements; version 1 does not.

answers.text: The network prefix carried with the packet
answers.rationale: The router has no knowledge of what Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) prefix was originally applied to the address.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must split two address blocks into smaller departmental networks: one block starting with 172.16 and one block starting with 230 for a video streaming group. Before borrowing any host bits, MSgt Rush checks what each block offers for subnetting. The 172.16 block passes the check. Which statement about the 230 block is correct?

answers.text: It keeps a default mask of 255.255.255.0
answers.rationale: A default mask belongs to Class A, B and C addresses; a block starting with 230 is outside those classes.

answers.text: It is written with a /4 network prefix
answers.rationale: A network prefix describes a mask, and addresses starting with 230 are described as having no subnet masks.

answers.text: It possesses no subnet mask at all
answers.rationale: Addresses starting with 230 are Class D, which does not possess any subnet masks and cannot be subnetted.

answers.text: It borrows host bits like the 172.16 block
answers.rationale: Borrowing host bits applies only to Class A, B and C addresses, so this block cannot be divided that way.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reviews a subnetting plan for a Class C network. One subnet is meant to hold a single sensor, so the plan gives it the mask 255.255.255.255, and the plan notes that this mask still begins with the default Class C mask. MSgt Rush marks the mask invalid under the subnetting rules. Which rule makes this mask invalid?

answers.text: That value is the broadcast address
answers.rationale: The subnetting rules state that a mask cannot be 255.255.255.255 because that value is the broadcast address.

answers.text: The start of the default mask is fixed
answers.rationale: The plan keeps the beginning of the default Class C mask, so this rule is met, not broken.

answers.text: That value is reserved for the network ID
answers.rationale: The network ID is the first host ID of a subnet, not a mask value.
Classes must start with their default mask; through subnetting the mask may then change.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush explains a subnet example to an airman: a company network is divided so that marketing computers see only marketing printers and sales computers see only sales printers. Each device gets an Internet Protocol (IP) address that logically associates it with the others on the same subnet, so devices on one subnet are not confused with those on the other. Which part of the example is called the hosts?

answers.rationale: The marketing and sales departments are the logical subnets of the company network.

answers.text: The company that holds both groups
answers.rationale: The company is the network that is divided into subnets.

answers.text: The email programs and the servers
answers.rationale: Email programs talking to servers illustrate why things need addresses; they are not the devices named in this example.
In terms of Internet Protocol (IP) addressing and subnets, the devices on each subnet, its computers and printers, are hosts.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must address one network that needs about 900 hosts. The block first offered holds more than 16,000 addresses, so most of them would sit unused. MSgt Rush instead takes a block sized much closer to the 900 hosts, keeps one mask for the whole network, and does not divide any subnet further. Which method allocates the address space this way?

keywords.text: one mask for the whole network

answers.rationale: Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) lets an admin carve out a number of host addresses closer to what is required.
This method gives one network more than one subnet mask by subnetting a subnet, which the plan does not do.
Fixed length masking breaks a network apart into equal subnets; the plan sizes one block for one network.
Address classes set the block sizes that waste addresses here; classes are no longer used except to teach basics.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush maintains a small training network in which every workstation taps directly into one shared cable that has exactly two endpoints; no hub or switch is used. A cart crushes the cable near one end, and MSgt Rush must record the layout's name and the trouble to expect while finding the fault. Which entry should MSgt Rush record?

answers.text: Bus; the problem can be difficult to isolate
answers.rationale: A bus has one central medium with exactly two endpoints; when it breaks the whole network fails, and isolating the problem can be difficult.

answers.text: Star; no connected node can reach the hub
answers.rationale: This layout has no central hub or switch, so hub failure does not describe it.
A tree joins star-configured segments to a backbone; this layout has no segments.

answers.text: Bus; just the nearest node goes down
answers.rationale: When the central bus breaks down, the whole network fails, not a single node.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush prices two layouts for one office. In Layout 1, all data passes through one central switch to every peripheral node. In Layout 2, every node taps into one shared cable with two endpoints. MSgt Rush must note the name and the cabling trait of Layout 1 on the quote. Which note is correct?

answers.text: Bus; it requires less cable length
answers.rationale: Less cable length is the trait of a shared cable with two endpoints, which is Layout 2.

answers.text: Tree; its cable costs tend to be higher
answers.rationale: A tree joins star segments to a backbone; Layout 1 has a single central switch only.

answers.text: Star; it requires less cable length
answers.rationale: Requiring less cable length than some other topologies is listed for the bus, not this layout.

answers.text: Star; its cable costs tend to be higher
answers.rationale: A central hub or switch with peripheral nodes is a star, and cable costs tend to be higher for star networks.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans links among five sites. Each site exchanges heavy traffic with all four other sites, so MSgt Rush links each site to the sites it interacts with most. When the plan is drawn, each site has its own direct link to each of the other four sites. Which topology does the drawing show?

answers.rationale: A partial mesh leaves some nodes without direct links to others; here no site lacks a direct link.
No central hub or switch carries all the data between the sites.
When each node is directly connected to every other node, the topology is a full mesh.
No linear backbone joins star-configured segments in this plan.

questions.stem: On each floor of a building, MSgt Rush wires the workstations to their own floor switch. The floor switches all attach to one linear backbone cable that runs from the basement to the roof. MSgt Rush must label the drawing with the topology of the whole network and the name for each floor group. Which label is correct?

answers.text: Hybrid; each floor group is a segment
answers.rationale: A combination of bus and star is a tree; only other combinations are called hybrid.

answers.text: Tree; each floor group is a partial mesh
answers.rationale: Each floor group connects workstations to one switch, which is a star configuration, not a mesh.

answers.text: Tree; each floor group is a segment
answers.rationale: Star-configured groups called segments on a linear bus backbone form a tree topology.

answers.text: Hybrid; each floor group is a subnet
answers.rationale: A bus and star combination is not called hybrid, and the floor groups are named for their physical layout.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush maps a base network for its physical diagram. Four core routers are each linked directly to every other core router. Each building connects to one of those routers through its own central switch, and the drawing seems to branch out from the core like a tree. Which topology name fits the whole network?

answers.rationale: A tree is only the combination of bus and star; this network has no linear bus backbone.
A combination of topologies that is not bus with star, here mesh with star, is a hybrid topology.
Only the core routers are fully meshed; the buildings hang off central switches.
The buildings use central switches, but the core links are not part of a star.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush draws a physical diagram for a long warehouse. A workstation at the far end will connect over Cat5e to a switch near the entrance, and several other Cat5e runs share the same floor. MSgt Rush must note on the diagram the span that the Cat5e limit covers and the risk of going past it. Which note is correct?

answers.text: Collisions beyond 100 meters of total cabling
answers.rationale: The limit is not a total for all cabling, and the risk named is degradation of the signal.

answers.text: Signal degradation beyond 100 meters between devices
answers.rationale: Cat5e is limited to 100 meters (328 feet) between devices; past the maximum distance a cable suffers signal degradation.

answers.text: Signal degradation beyond 100 meters per floor
answers.rationale: The limit is measured between devices, not for all the runs on a floor.
Collisions come from devices transmitting at the same time, not from exceeding a cable's maximum distance.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush adds one fiber optic run and several twisted pair runs to a physical network diagram. The fiber run must use one of several connector types, and every run must use the proper cable type for its distance. MSgt Rush needs one reference that covers the connector types and is used to ensure proper cable type and distance. Which reference fits?

answers.rationale: A logical network diagram shows subnets, routers, firewalls and routing protocols, not connector types.

answers.text: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.3 rules
answers.rationale: These rules define how devices detect and respond to collisions, not connector types or cable distance.
A procedure specification details the actual procedures for a task, not cabling.
These standards are used when developing physical diagrams to ensure proper cable type and distance, and they cover connector types.

questions.stem: During an outage, MSgt Rush must find which subnet a router interface sits in and which routing protocol runs between two routers. The cable runs and hardware locations are already known. MSgt Rush must pull the right drawing and note which layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model that drawing correlates with. Which entry is correct?

answers.rationale: Logical network diagrams show subnets and routing protocols and correlate with layer 3, the network layer.
Level 2 shows the data links between adjacent nodes, not the information in this drawing.
A physical diagram shows cables and hardware like a floorplan, which MSgt Rush already knows.
A data flow diagram shows data sources, flows, stores and transformations, not subnets and routing protocols.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush rebuilds an office network. Before the change, every workstation tapped into one shared cable with exactly two endpoints. After the change, every workstation runs to one central switch. The network uses the Ethernet protocol to define the path for transferring packets both before and after. Which pair describes how the physical and logical topologies changed?

answers.text: Physical bus to star; logical bus to star
answers.rationale: The logical topology is bound to network protocols, and the protocol did not change, so the logical layout did not follow the cabling.

answers.text: Physical stays bus; logical bus to star
answers.rationale: The cabling did change, and the logical topology is bound to the protocol rather than the cabling.

answers.text: Physical bus to tree; logical stays bus
answers.rationale: A single central switch with its workstations is a star; a tree needs star groups on a linear backbone.

answers.text: Physical bus to star; logical stays bus
answers.rationale: Cabling moved from bus to star, while Ethernet, the best-known logical bus, kept the logical topology a bus.

questions.stem: On a wired Ethernet network cabled as a physical star around one central switch, an airman's workstation sends data meant for a printer. Three other workstations are connected to the same network. MSgt Rush must describe what happens to the data under the network's logical topology. Which description is correct?

answers.text: The printer keeps it; the others ignore it
answers.rationale: In a logical bus the data is broadcast to the entire network; each device looks, keeps data meant for it and ignores the rest.

answers.text: The printer keeps it; the others forward it on
answers.rationale: Devices that find the data is not for them ignore it rather than passing it along.

answers.text: The switch delivers it to the printer
answers.rationale: In a logical bus, each time a device has data to send, it broadcasts the data to the entire network.

answers.text: The printer keeps it; the others return it
answers.rationale: Devices that find the data is not for them ignore it rather than sending it back.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush documents the access method of an Ethernet network. All computers check the cable for traffic before sending a frame, and rules define how they detect and respond to collisions. MSgt Rush must record where Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (CSMA/CD) sits in the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model. Which entry is correct?

answers.text: Originates at Physical; implemented at Data Link
answers.rationale: The order is reversed: the method starts at the higher of these two layers.

answers.text: Originates and implemented at Data Link
answers.rationale: The method is implemented at a lower layer than the one where it originates.

answers.text: Originates at Data Link; implemented at Physical
answers.rationale: Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (CSMA/CD) originates at the Data Link layer and is implemented at the Physical layer.

answers.text: Originates at Network; implemented at Data Link
answers.rationale: The network layer deals with packet forwarding through routers, not this access method.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush draws a data flow diagram for a base maintenance system. Within the system, one step takes incoming work orders and turns them into a weekly report. The report goes to a records office that lies outside the system boundary, where the reports are kept for years. Which pair of symbols fits the step and the records office?

answers.rationale: The step changes incoming data into outgoing data, so it is more than movement of data.
The office keeps records, but it lies outside the system boundary, so it is not a repository inside the system.
A process transforms incoming data flow into outgoing data flow; a destination outside the system boundary is an external entity.
The step changes the data rather than holding data that is not moving.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush briefs a data flow diagram of the whole base system at a wing meeting. Then MSgt Rush gives the airmen who run one portion a separate diagram of that portion at greater detail, so each level of authority reviews the view that fits it. This practice is called leveling. Which other name does it go by?

answers.rationale: Segments are the star-configured groups of a tree topology, not detail levels of a diagram.
The process of representing different detail levels is called leveling or partitioning.
Repetition, how many times a procedure is performed, is not included on a data flow diagram.
The context diagram is Level 0, one level of the diagram, not the practice of showing several levels.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares a legacy hub with a switch. Which capability do hubs not provide on the network?

answers.rationale: Hubs repeat frames out ports, so they do provide this.
Bandwidth is shared on a hub.
Hubs provide neither security nor identification of connected devices.
Hubs copy frames to the other interfaces.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush makes configuration changes on a switch. Which file, kept in the running memory, stores those changes?

answers.rationale: Changes are stored in a file called running-configuration.
The startup file is kept in Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM).
The Operating System (OS) is saved in flash memory.

A snap-in is an administrative tool hosted in a console.
A batch file is a script that automates tasks.

questions.reviewCue: Think of a cook actually preparing a dish, as opposed to the recipe card that sits on the shelf.

questions.stem: Which Windows tool was the first built in to automate routine tasks, such as user account management or nightly backups, with batch (.bat) files?

answers.rationale: It extends the first shell and was not the first.
It gives an overview of the system and does not run batch files.
It was the first shell built in to automate routine tasks with batch files.
It lists services and does not run batch files.

questions.reviewCue: Like the original hand tool in the toolbox that later power tools were built to extend.

questions.stem: Which Windows shell was designed to extend the Command shell with a more extensible scripting language?

answers.rationale: It is the original shell that was extended.
It runs scripts but is not the shell that extends the original.
It gives an overview of the system and is not a shell.
It extends the capabilities of the Command shell.

questions.reviewCue: Like an upgraded workshop that keeps every old tool and adds a smarter set beside them.

questions.stem: Which type of server process carries out the real tasks on the server, activating and executing them and monitoring them until they are finished?

answers.rationale: Work processes do the actual server work and monitor tasks until finished.
A communication process is another server process type, but it does not execute the tasks.
Startup is when processes begin, not a type of server process.

questions.reviewCue: Like the crew on the factory floor who build, run, and check each job until it ships.

questions.stem: Which kind of server process handles central tasks that must not be allocated, such as time basis and process administration?

keywords.text: central tasks that must not be allocated

answers.rationale: A communication process is another server process type, but it does not handle central tasks.
It is used for special tasks that must not be allocated.
No agent process appears among the server process types; agents are not server processes.
No interface process appears among the server process types; user interfaces are not server processes.

questions.reviewCue: Like the shift lead who keeps the clock and the schedule that the rest of the crew cannot split up.

questions.stem: Which type of server process holds the connections to the agents and the user interfaces?

answers.rationale: A work process is another server process type, but it does not hold these connections.
A primary work process is one of the work processes; it does not hold these connections.
These processes hold the connections to the agents and user interfaces.

questions.reviewCue: Like the switchboard operator who links every caller to the right desk without doing the desk work.

questions.stem: Which Task Manager tab breaks down how everything on the system is currently performing and shows how system resources are being used?

answers.rationale: It lists background services and not the resource breakdown.
It lists signed-in accounts and not the resource breakdown.
It shows app use over time and not the current breakdown.
It breaks down how everything on the system is currently performing.

questions.reviewCue: Like a gauge board that shows which running job is eating the most fuel right now.

questions.stem: A section's network mixes thin clients that have little or no storage with thick clients and workstations. MSgt Rush needs one host on the Local Area Network (LAN) that many of these remote computers can reach at the same moment, acting as their connection point and supplying applications and shared resources to them. Which server fits this role?

answers.rationale: Correct: a terminal server is the connection point that supplies applications and resources to thin clients, thick clients, and workstations.
Wrong: a Telnet server lets a user log on remotely, but it is not described as the connection point for client types.
Wrong: a virtual server converts one physical server into Virtual Machines (VMs); it is not described as a client connection point.
Wrong: an application server is middleware that runs specific programs; it is not described as the connection point for remote clients.

questions.stem: An outside scan shows that the Internet can see the address of every workstation on a squadron network. The same week, an airman downloads files from a site that is not authorized. MSgt Rush wants a single server placed in the path of outbound requests that deals with both problems. Which server should MSgt Rush add?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a Domain Name System (DNS) server translates domain names to addresses; it neither hides addresses nor blocks sites.
Correct: a proxy server can hide the addresses of network devices from the Internet and prohibit access to unauthorized sites.
Wrong: a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server assigns addresses; it does not hide them or filter downloads.
Wrong: an Active Directory (AD) server stores information about network resources; it does not sit in the path of outbound requests.

questions.stem: Every workstation in a shop already has its Internet Protocol (IP) address and can reach other hosts. When an airman types the site's numeric address into a browser, the page loads, but typing rhope-ops.github.io/icf gives an error. MSgt Rush suspects one server has stopped doing its job for the shop. Which server is the most likely cause?

answers.rationale: Wrong: the workstations already hold their addresses, so the server that assigns them is working.
Wrong: the page loads by its numeric address, so the server holding the site data is working.
Correct: a Domain Name System (DNS) server translates domain names such as rhope-ops.github.io to Internet Protocol (IP) addresses.
Wrong: the same site loads by its numeric address, so no filter is blocking it; only the name fails.

questions.stem: Twenty new laptops arrive for a section network. MSgt Rush does not want to type an Internet Protocol (IP) address into each laptop by hand, and the commander also wants a record of the laptops' network connections afterward. Which single server covers both needs?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a Domain Name System (DNS) server translates names to addresses; it does not give each laptop an address.
Wrong: a Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server handles mail; it neither hands out addresses nor tracks connections.
Wrong: a File Transfer Protocol (FTP) server moves files between computers; it does not assign addresses.
Correct: a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server assigns addresses automatically and also logs and tracks network connections.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must send a folder of 40 large maintenance logs from a computer in one shop to a computer in another shop. Attaching the logs to messages is too slow, and the logs must not be posted for browsers to load. The move should keep the logs organized and let MSgt Rush control the transfer. Which server suits this task?

answers.rationale: Correct: a File Transfer Protocol (FTP) server moves one or more files between computers with organization and transfer control.
Wrong: a Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server transfers and stores mail, and attaching the logs to messages was ruled out.
Wrong: a Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) server delivers site data to browsers, and posting the logs for browsers was ruled out.
Wrong: a cloud server delivers pooled resources from a provider; it is not described as moving files between two computers.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is setting up a server that will transfer and store messages for a wing across its Local Area Networks (LANs), its Wide Area Networks (WANs), and the Internet. Before opening the firewall, MSgt Rush must know which protocol this server uses for that traffic. Which protocol should MSgt Rush plan for?

answers.rationale: Wrong: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) carries communication between browsers and web servers, not stored messages.
Correct: mail servers, which transfer and store mail across networks and the Internet, use Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP).
Wrong: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) moves files between computers; it is not the protocol mail servers use.
Wrong: the Telnet protocol lets users log on to a remote computer; it does not carry stored messages.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's unit owns one physical server in an off-site data center and manages its hardware itself, with no outside provider. Three sections each want to administer their own system services as if they had complete control of a server, and their workloads shift every week. Which approach meets these needs?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a cloud server and its infrastructure are managed by the cloud provider, but this unit manages its own hardware.
Wrong: a terminal server supplies applications to remote clients; it does not give each section control of its own server.
Correct: a virtual server converts one physical server into multiple Virtual Machines (VMs), each administered as if in complete control.
Wrong: a multi-purpose server performs several functions, but the sections would share one system rather than each controlling its own.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush watches network traffic while an airman opens the base's home page. The browser sends a request, and the server loads a file from its disk and transfers it across the network back to the browser. MSgt Rush needs to name the protocol that carries this exchange between the browser and the server. Which protocol is it?

answers.rationale: Wrong: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) moves files between computers, but it is not described for browser requests to web servers.
Wrong: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the protocol mail servers use, not browsers.
Wrong: the Telnet protocol lets users log on to a remote computer and run programs, not load web pages.
Correct: communication between a client's browser and a web server uses Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP).

questions.stem: A squadron needs processing power, storage, and applications that many airmen can reach on demand from anywhere, delivered remotely over the Internet. MSgt Rush has no staff to maintain hardware, so the squadron must not have to manage the server or any of the infrastructure behind it. Which server type fits this need?

answers.rationale: Correct: a cloud server and all associated infrastructure are managed by the cloud provider, such as Microsoft Azure.
Wrong: a virtual server lets each section administer its own services, which still leaves the squadron managing them.
Wrong: a terminal server is a host on the Local Area Network (LAN) that the squadron would run itself.
Wrong: an application server runs specific programs as middleware; it is not described as managed by an outside provider.

questions.stem: A plant runs a self-contained industrial network with no link to outside networks. MSgt Rush needs to log on remotely from one computer to the plant's devices and execute tasks on them as if sitting at each machine. Because the network is closed, a server type with a known security weakness is acceptable here. Which server type is typically used in this setting?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a terminal server supplies applications to thin clients and workstations; it is not described as limited to industrial networks.
Correct: a Telnet server is typically used only in industrial and self-contained networks because it is not secure.
Wrong: a virtual server re-creates a physical server as Virtual Machines (VMs); it does not provide remote logon to devices.
Wrong: a proxy server mediates between clients and external servers, and this network has no outside link.

questions.stem: A small detachment has one server for six airmen. It hosts the detachment's website, it also handles all printing on the local network, and MSgt Rush sits at it each morning to do administrator work. A new airman asks how to describe this server's role on the network. Which description fits it?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a single-purpose server provides specific services and nothing else, and end users do not sit at it.
Wrong: it does host a website, but a web server alone serves only web pages, not printing and administrator work.
Correct: a multi-purpose (non-dedicated) web server may also act as a print server or the administrator's workstation.
Wrong: a workstation is a personal computer used by a client; this machine serves the site and printing to others.

questions.stem: Five airmen at a deployed site link their laptops with no server present. Each laptop shares one folder with the others while keeping the rest of its files inaccessible, and when one laptop requests a file from another, the second laptop answers as the server. No laptop has more authority than another. Which network model are the airmen using?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a client-server model relies on a dedicated server as intermediary, and this site has no server.
Wrong: a multi-purpose server is one server doing several tasks, but this site has no server at all.
Wrong: a terminal server is a host that clients connect through; no such host exists here.
Correct: in a peer-to-peer model there are no dedicated servers, and each computer can share only some of its resources.

questions.stem: An airman will be posted for weeks at a remote site that has no network and no domain at all. MSgt Rush must issue a device that has its own processor, memory, and drive and that will never connect to a central server during that time. Which device can function completely on its own in that setting?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a thin client relies on the central server for applications, processing, and memory.
Correct: a workstation has all components and can function completely independently of a server or network.
Wrong: a thick client works in a client-server configuration and still pulls data from the central server occasionally.
Wrong: a terminal server is a host that supplies applications to remote clients; it is not a device issued to an airman.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush checks an airman's workstation while it runs a mission planning application opened through a web portal. Only screen images, mouse movements, and keystrokes cross the network, the workstation's processor shows no load from the application, and the whole squadron uses the one copy installed on a shared Windows server. Which desktop virtualization type is in use?

keywords.text: one copy installed on a shared Windows server

answers.rationale: Only the graphical interface, mouse, and keyboard are shared, with no processing on the client and one shared application instance.
This type hosts a dedicated Operating System (OS) Virtual Machine (VM) for each client, not one shared copy.
This model sends portions of the program code to the client, so the client would show processing.
This type moves profiles, settings, and data to a central share; it is not an application delivery method.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must give deployed airmen access to graphics-heavy imagery software from tablets. The design needs hardware-based Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) sharing through a secure connection from any device, and each airman's desktop must stay totally separate from every other desktop on the server, with permissions customized for each airman. Which desktop virtualization type fits?

answers.text: Presentation virtualization on a shared Virtual Machine (VM)
answers.rationale: This type has users share one application instance on a shared server, so desktops are not separate.
Its hypervisor hosts a dedicated machine per client and enables hardware-based Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) sharing from any device.
This type decouples profiles and data from the Operating System (OS); it does not host separate desktops.
This model delivers program portions on demand to a client; it does not host separate desktops.

questions.stem: An airman works at a physical desktop in the squadron office on Monday, a virtual desktop from a deployed laptop on Wednesday, and a different physical workstation on Friday. MSgt Rush wants the airman's settings and data kept in a central data share and applied at every one of these, including the physical machines. Which approach meets this need?

answers.rationale: This type hosts dedicated Virtual Machines (VM) on a server; it does not reach the physical desktops.
This type shows a shared server application to clients; it does not manage profiles on physical desktops.
It decouples profile, settings, and data from the Operating System (OS), stores them centrally, and also works on physical desktops.
This type runs applications from central servers; it does not store a person's settings and data centrally.

questions.stem: An airman launches a large engineering program on a laptop that never had it installed. A packet capture shows only a small part of the program's code arriving at first, with more portions sent across the network when the airman opens other features. The program then runs on the laptop's own processor. Which delivery model is MSgt Rush seeing?

keywords.text: small part of the program's code

answers.rationale: This type processes nothing on the client and sends only a picture of the application.
This type runs applications on central servers and serves them up, rather than sending code portions on demand.
This type hosts a full dedicated desktop Virtual Machine (VM) on a server for each client.
Most applications need only a small portion of their code, so portions are offered across the network whenever required.

questions.stem: A flight line test set uses older industrial software that runs only on a legacy Operating System (OS). MSgt Rush must move the workstation to a current OS that receives up-to-date security patches, keep using the old software, and be able to transfer that software between computers on removable media without installing it. Which approach meets all three needs?

answers.rationale: It runs applications in foreign environments, keeps the new patched Operating System (OS), and makes them portable on removable media.
This architecture modifies a guest kernel for hyper calls; it does not make software portable on removable media.
This architecture presents emulated devices such as a switch to a guest server, not portable legacy software.
This model sends program portions across a network on demand; it does not carry software on removable media.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must run twenty small Linux web applications on one Linux server. Each application needs isolation from the others, new instances must come online extremely fast from the same base set, and no application needs its own full copy of an Operating System (OS). Which approach should MSgt Rush choose?

answers.rationale: Each of these replicates an entire Operating System (OS) for its application, so each is larger and slower to bring online.
They share one host kernel, spin up from the same base set very fast, and still isolate applications.
Each guest still runs its own modified Operating System (OS) kernel inside a Virtual Machine (VM).
This architecture presents emulated hardware to a guest server; it does not remove the guest Operating System (OS).

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans to move several web services off their Virtual Machines (VM) onto one server whose host kernel allows multiple isolated user-space instances, to gain efficiency. The services run different software stacks today. An airman asks what flexibility the squadron gives up in exchange for that efficiency. Which limitation comes with this architecture?

answers.text: The guest kernel must be modified for hyper calls
answers.rationale: Modified guest kernels that use hyper calls belong to para-virtualization, a different architecture.

answers.text: The hypervisor steals resources from its guests
answers.rationale: Resource stealing is a drawback of a hosted Type 2 hypervisor running on a busy host Operating System (OS).

answers.text: Each instance must match the host server's system
answers.rationale: This method gives greater efficiency but less flexibility: the container Operating System (OS) must match the host server's.

answers.text: Built-in device drivers limit the hardware support
answers.rationale: Limited built-in device drivers are a drawback of a bare-metal Type 1 hypervisor.

questions.stem: A training network needs a router between two subnets, but the squadron has no budget to buy, power, and maintain another physical device. MSgt Rush sets up the server so that the hypervisor presents a router to one guest virtual server, no matter what physical hardware is installed in the host. Which server virtualization architecture is this?

answers.rationale: This lets a guest reach real host hardware through hyper calls; it does not present a simulated device.
This creates isolated user-space instances on a shared kernel; it does not present a simulated router.
This pools disks from several network storage devices; it does not present a router to a guest.
The host or hypervisor emulates hardware such as a router for the guest, saving the physical device's costs.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares two Virtual Machines (VM) on one host. In the first, the guest Operating System (OS) is completely isolated and never interacts with the hypervisor. In the second, the guest kernel was modified, is not fully separate from the host, and processes faster by using host hardware directly. Which technique does the second machine use?

answers.rationale: Its modified guest kernel talks to the host through hyper calls, speeding processing by using host hardware directly.
This describes the first machine: the guest is completely isolated and does not interact with the hypervisor.
This presents emulated devices to a guest; it does not modify the guest kernel.
This uses containers on a shared host kernel, with no guest Operating System (OS) inside a Virtual Machine (VM).

questions.stem: An airman must test a software update against a copy of the base network, including several servers, a firewall, and workstations. The squadron has only one spare server, will not buy specialized servers for occasional testing, and the live network must not be touched. Which virtual environment does MSgt Rush set up for the airman?

answers.rationale: This is a copy of one Virtual Machine (VM) at a point in time, not a replica of a network.
It is a simulated lab reflecting a real network, replicating several machines on a single piece of hardware.
This separates applications on one shared kernel; it does not reflect a whole physical network.
This lets software pick the best physical server for a Virtual Machine (VM) image; it is not a test network.

questions.stem: Three Virtual Machines (VM) on separate physical hosts run the same squadron application. Monitoring shows one machine overloaded and slow to respond while the other two sit idle. MSgt Rush wants the regular workload divided so every machine carries a portion and the machines adjust dynamically to the application's demands. Which application of virtualization should MSgt Rush apply?

answers.rationale: This moves once-dedicated servers onto fewer hosts; it does not divide work among existing machines.
This lets software pick the best physical server for a Virtual Machine (VM) image, not divide regular work.
It divides the regular workload among machines on separate hardware so none sit idle and responsiveness improves.
This responds to catastrophic losses such as a whole data center, not an uneven daily workload.

questions.stem: A squadron runs twelve physical servers, each with one function such as a domain controller or a name server, and most of them sit underutilized. MSgt Rush must cut the number of machines to maintain and put existing resources to better use, so the twelve servers become Virtual Machines (VM) on one host. Which application of virtualization is this?

answers.rationale: This spreads one workload across machines on separate hardware; it does not reduce the number of servers.
This points software at a Virtual Machine (VM) image to pick a server; it does not merge servers.
This responds to catastrophic incidents such as losing a data center, not to underutilized servers.
One host now holds many once-dedicated, underutilized servers, increasing utilization and cutting maintenance costs.

questions.stem: On Monday one Virtual Machine (VM) crashed and was restarted, and on Tuesday a failed server's work shifted to another host with no outage. On Wednesday MSgt Rush writes a plan for a flood that could permanently destroy the entire base data center, relying on machine images captured in files. Which area does Wednesday's plan cover?

answers.rationale: It covers incidents far worse than a single crash or hardware failure, such as an entire data center lost.
This explains Tuesday's event, where the work shifted between machines on separate hardware.
This lets software pick a physical server for an image; it is not a plan for catastrophic loss.
This returns one machine to an earlier state, fitting a single crash rather than a lost data center.

questions.stem: An airman deletes a Virtual Machine (VM) that nobody could explain, and a squadron service goes down. MSgt Rush finds the host now holds far more machines than the squadron can manage, many of them unused, while storage, bandwidth, and electricity use keep climbing. Which problem has the squadron run into?

answers.text: A Virtual Machine (VM) patch management gap
answers.rationale: Missed patches expose security issues; they do not explain more machines than the squadron can track.
Machines created over time exceed management capacity, their functions are lost, and unused machines drain resources.
Change control governs approval of infrastructure changes; it does not describe too many machines to manage.
Load balancing divides work among machines; it does not create unmanaged, unused machines.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's team patched the host and guest Operating Systems (OS), the web servers, and the database servers on schedule. A month later, an attacker gets in through a small open-source library bundled inside a third-party reporting tool on a guest. Logs captured the attack, and every change had been approved. Which area of virtualization security fell short?

answers.rationale: Every change had been approved, so the change control process worked as intended.
The logs captured the attack, so the audit trail did its job.
Updates focused on big targets while smaller third-party and open-source components were forgotten.
Nothing shows wrong host accounts or access; the attacker came in through a neglected component.

questions.stem: An airman's desktop has uncommon hardware whose drivers come only with its installed Operating System (OS). The airman must keep that OS and add a Virtual Machine (VM) that runs a different OS for a Windows-only tool, accepting some loss of VM performance. Which choice fits this desktop?

answers.rationale: This installs directly on hardware in place of the host Operating System (OS) and has limited built-in drivers.
Containers share the host kernel, so they cannot run a different Operating System (OS) than the host.
This modifies a guest kernel for hyper calls; it does not leave the installed Operating System (OS) handling drivers.
It runs on the host Operating System (OS), which handles drivers, giving better hardware compatibility but degraded performance.

questions.stem: A server runs a Type 1 hypervisor that hosts a Virtual Machine (VM) with a Linux distribution as its guest Operating System (OS). Inside that VM, MSgt Rush creates several containers that all share the Linux kernel. An airman asks how the Linux OS should be described in relation to those containers. Which term applies?

answers.rationale: The Linux guest serves as the host Operating System (OS) for containers that share its kernel.
Nothing here runs on top of the Linux system to create Virtual Machines (VM); the containers share its kernel.
The bare-metal role belongs to the Type 1 hypervisor installed on the server hardware.
Para-virtualization modifies a guest kernel for hyper calls; it does not describe the containers' shared kernel.

questions.stem: A host server runs today with only two of one component, which works but falls below the recommended amount. MSgt Rush must now place its Virtual Machines (VM) on three separate networks, keep service if one link fails, and raise speed and bandwidth. Which component should MSgt Rush add to the host?

answers.rationale: This card connects a monitor when a host lacks integrated graphics; it does not separate traffic or add redundancy.
Two can operate a host, but more are recommended for bandwidth, redundancy, speed, and separating traffic.
These raise processor efficiency for virtualization; they do not split traffic onto separate networks.
Storage limits how many machines are stored and run; it does not separate traffic or add redundancy.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush supports a forest with two domains. Each domain controller holds the objects and object attributes unique to its own domain. Airmen in the first domain now need to locate and use a shared printer published in the second domain. Which server must MSgt Rush make sure is available so that computers in one domain can find resources in the other?

keywords.text: shared printer published in the second domain

answers.rationale: A member server serves dedicated purposes such as file and print; it does not locate objects across domains.
It holds a partial replica of every object in every domain of the forest, so computers in one domain can locate resources in another.
Each domain controller holds only objects unique to its own domain, so it alone cannot locate the second domain's printer.
A domain client is a computer that uses resources; it does not let other computers locate resources in other domains.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush supports one domain whose users work at two bases. A slow Wide Area Network (WAN) link joins the two bases, and each base has its own squadrons and administrators. MSgt Rush wants every user to stay in the same domain while Active Directory (AD) reflects the slow link between the bases. Which component should MSgt Rush create for each base?

answers.rationale: Windows encourages sites when a network is divided by a slow link, and both sites can be part of the same domain.
A child domain would split the users into separate domains, but they must stay in one domain.
A domain tree is a collection of domains sharing a namespace; it does not reflect a slow link inside one domain.
A forest is the collection of domain trees at the top of the structure; it does not mark a slow link.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush joins a new Windows Server to the squadron's domain so that it can host the squadron's web pages. The server must belong to the domain, but it must not hold a writable copy of the domain's Active Directory (AD) information and must not authenticate logons. Which role should MSgt Rush give the new server?

answers.rationale: Every domain controller holds a complete, writable copy of the domain's directory information and authenticates users.
A global catalog server is normally a domain controller and stores replicas of directory objects.
A domain client runs a user's desktop environment to reach resources; it does not host web pages for the squadron.
It belongs to a domain without being the domain controller and is used for dedicated purposes such as web servers.

questions.stem: A small base runs one domain with a single domain controller, plus a member server for file and print services. When the domain controller fails, no airman can log on to the domain, though the file server keeps running. MSgt Rush wants the next failure of one server to leave domain logons working. Which addition does MSgt Rush need?

keywords.text: no airman can log on to the domain

answers.rationale: A member server is not a domain controller, so it cannot authenticate users when the only one fails.
A site maps the physical structure of the network; adding one does not add a server that authenticates users.
Networks normally have more than one, so if one fails others store the directory structure and authenticate users.
A domain tree is a collection of domains sharing a namespace; it adds no backup for this domain's logons.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush changes the replication topology data on a domain controller in AF.Domain. Later, MSgt Rush signs on to a domain controller in Medical.Domain, a different domain in the same forest, and finds the same change there. Which directory partition holds the data that MSgt Rush changed?

answers.rationale: It contains replication topology data replicated throughout the forest, and every domain controller in the forest has a replica.
The domain partition stores users, computers, and groups for one specific domain, not data shared by another domain.
The schema partition stores class and attribute definitions for objects, not replication topology data.
The forest root domain is the first domain created in the forest; it is not a directory partition.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must add a badge number to the types of information that a user account object can hold. The change has to reach every user object in the forest, existing and future, not only the users of one domain or one Organizational Unit (OU). Which part of Active Directory (AD) defines this for the user object type?

answers.rationale: The configuration partition stores configuration objects and replication topology, not the definition of a user object type.
Each type of object is defined through it, the template of attributes that sets the types of information an object can hold.
The domain partition stores the users and other objects of one domain, not the definitions of object types.
An Organizational Unit (OU) holds users, groups, and computers; it does not define what a user object can hold.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush creates user accounts for two airmen in one Organizational Unit (OU). Both accounts are user objects of the same type, and Active Directory (AD) keeps them as two separate entities. MSgt Rush reviews their attributes to see how AD distinguishes the two objects. Which statement describes what MSgt Rush finds?

keywords.text: user objects of the same type

answers.rationale: All objects of the same type or class have the same set of attributes.
Objects of the same class are distinguished from each other by having different values for at least one attribute.
Syntaxes belong to the schema for the object type, and both objects share that same type.
Some attributes, such as First Name for a user object, are required to have values.

questions.stem: In an Organizational Unit (OU), MSgt Rush finds a printer object and several user objects. MSgt Rush tries to move one of the user objects into the printer object, but Active Directory (AD) does not allow it, although moving the same user object into another OU works. Which description fits the printer object?

keywords.text: move one of the user objects into the printer object

answers.rationale: A container object can hold other objects, but the printer object could not hold the user object.
A child domain is a domain created after the root, and domains are container objects that hold other objects.
It is found in containers such as Organizational Units (OUs) and cannot contain other directory objects.
The forest root is the first domain created in the forest, and domains can hold other objects.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is deploying a new Active Directory (AD) forest for a base. The plan calls for one domain used only to administer the forest and three regional domains for the squadrons, each with its own Organizational Units (OUs). Before building any of the regional domains, which domain must MSgt Rush already have created?

keywords.text: building any of the regional domains

answers.rationale: It must be created before any of the regional domains and provides the foundation for the infrastructure.
Child domains are created after the root, so a regional child domain cannot come before it.
A domain tree is a collection of domains, not a single domain that must exist before the regional ones.
Squadron domains are regional domains, and none of those may be built ahead of the foundation domain.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush manages two domain trees, AF.Domain and Medical.Domain, that share one global catalog and one directory schema. questions.stem: Which vulnerability is one of the easiest ways for adversaries to gather information about military operations?

answers.rationale: Social media is described as one of the easiest ways for adversaries to learn about military operations.
Open conversations let unauthorized listeners overhear work details, but they are not described as the easiest route.

answers.text: Family and friends without a need to know
answers.rationale: Discussing duties with family or friends is a risk, but it is not described as the easiest route.
Private and text messages can be intercepted, but they are not described as the easiest route.

questions.reviewCue: Anything you post can be read by the other side, so the safest post is the one you never make.

questions.stem: Which program uses measures and controls to deny unauthorized persons information derived from United States Government information systems related to national security?

answers.rationale: This program limits what adversaries can collect about friendly activities rather than denying persons information derived from government systems.
This program protects Air Force information systems and information, with a focus on end-point security and ports, protocols and services.
This program denies unauthorized persons national security information from government systems and ensures their authenticity.
This program identifies vulnerabilities that could lead to compromising emanations and their possible interception.

questions.reviewCue: The guard on the line: scrambling and safeguarding what travels between government systems so eavesdroppers learn nothing.

questions.stem: Which term names the restoration of encrypted data to its original plain text or other readily usable state?

answers.rationale: Encryption is the opposite step, converting plain text into a form unauthorized people cannot easily understand.
Cryptanalysis tries to break a coding system for an unauthorized user, rather than restoring data to readable form.
Cryptography is the use of coding systems to both encrypt and decrypt, not only the restoring step.
Decryption turns cipher text back into readable plain text.

questions.reviewCue: Unlocking the scrambled message so the intended reader sees the original wording again.

questions.stem: Which term names the science of trying to break a coding system so the information can be revealed to an unauthorized user?

answers.rationale: Cryptanalysis is the science of trying to break a coding system so protected information can be revealed.
Cryptography is the use of coding systems to encrypt and decrypt, not an attempt to break them.
Cryptosecurity is the protection from proper use of cryptographic systems, which works against attempts to break them.
Decryption is the restoration of encrypted data to readable form, not an attempt to break the coding system.

questions.reviewCue: The code-breaker trade: studying the other side scrambled messages to find the weakness that unlocks them.

questions.stem: Which component of Communications Security (COMSEC) is the protection that results from the proper use of cryptographic systems?

answers.rationale: Transmission Security protects intentional transmissions by choosing a secured system, rather than the proper use of cryptographic systems.
Physical security guards sensitive material with barriers, limited access and approved safes, not the proper use of cryptographic systems.
It is the protection from proper use of cryptographic systems, including making a strong system and using it correctly.
Red/black separation keeps plain-text signals apart from encrypted signals in cabling, not the proper use of cryptographic systems.

questions.reviewCue: A strong lock is useless if you leave it unlatched: this is about using the coding gear the right way.

questions.stem: Which component of Communications Security (COMSEC) makes personnel choose the right secured system, such as a secure telephone, for each communication need?

answers.rationale: Cryptosecurity covers the proper use of cryptographic systems, not the choice of secured system for a communication need.
It selects the proper secured method so intentional transmissions are protected from interception and exploitation.
Physical security covers barriers, limited access and approved safes, not the choice of communication system.
Red/black separation keeps plain-text signals apart from encrypted signals in cabling, not the choice of communication system.

questions.reviewCue: Pick the right pipe: even without scrambling, how a message is sent decides whether it can be intercepted.

questions.stem: Which component of Communications Security (COMSEC) addresses improper destruction of waste, improper handling and unauthorized viewing or possession of COMSEC material?

answers.rationale: Cryptosecurity covers the proper use of cryptographic systems, not waste destruction or unauthorized viewing.
Transmission Security covers choosing a proper secured system for communications, not waste destruction or unauthorized viewing.
Red/black separation keeps plain-text signals apart from encrypted signals, not waste destruction or unauthorized viewing.
It covers these additional threats to cryptographic material and is met with barriers, limited access and approved safes.

questions.reviewCue: Locks, shredders and clearances: the everyday habits that keep sensitive material from walking out or being glimpsed.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reviews an incident on a workstation within the base security perimeter. Someone logged on with an account the unit itself had granted and, using only the rights that account already held, copied files in a way the unit never approved. Which term names the source of this incident?

answers.rationale: An outside attack gains unauthorized or illegitimate entry, but this account was one the unit itself had granted.
A botnet of compromised computers serves outside attacks, but this incident began on a workstation within the base security perimeter.
Granted rights misused in a way the unit never approved, from a workstation within the perimeter, fit this threat agent.
Elevation of privilege lets someone do what they are not authorized to do, but only rights the account already held were used.

questions.stem: An approved duty schedule change goes out from an airman's account to his flight, and every reader is cleared to see it. Later he says someone else must have sent it from his account. Logon records show only his own card and code were used, at his own desk. Which item of the Microsoft threat model does this case show?

keywords.text: someone else must have sent it

answers.rationale: Spoofing is pretending to be someone else, but logon records show only his own card and code were used.
Tampering is modifying something, but this schedule change was an approved one.
Information disclosure gives information to someone not authorized to have it, but every reader was cleared to see it.
Denying an action that his own card and code performed is claiming he did not do something.

questions.stem: A base web host is hit with far more requests than it can answer, and legitimate users are shut out. The requests pour in at once from thousands of infected home machines that answer to one command server. Each request asks only for the public front page that anyone may view. Which attack is this?

answers.rationale: Floods of requests from thousands of infected machines under one command server, shutting out legitimate users, fit this many-machine attack usually performed by a botnet.

answers.text: Denial of Service from a single computer
answers.rationale: That standard attack comes from one computer, but these requests pour in from thousands of infected home machines.
A botnet is the group of infected machines sending the requests, not the attack that shuts out legitimate users.
Unauthorized access aims to reach a resource the host should not provide, but each request asks only for the public front page.

questions.stem: Three months later, an audit turns up a discrepancy in a finance system's books, and staff cannot tell how far back any figure can be trusted.
